translations.literal: Eunuchs, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs, Part One

translations.literal: ○ Dou Shenbao, Wang Renrui, Wang Jien, Li Shenfu
translations.idiomatic: Dou Shenbao, Wang Renrui, Wang Jien, and Li Shenfu

sentences.zh: （弟神祐）〉

translations.literal: (Younger brother Shen You))
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Shen You)

sentences.zh: 劉承規閻承翰秦翰周懷政張崇貴張繼能衛紹欽石知顒

translations.literal: Liu Chenggui, Yan Chenghan, Qin Han, Zhou Huaizheng, Zhang Chonggui, Zhang Jineng, Wei Shaoqin, Shi Zhiyong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chenggui, Yan Chenghan, Qin Han, Zhou Huaizheng, Zhang Chonggui, Zhang Jineng, Wei Shaoqin, and Shi Zhiyong

sentences.zh: 鄧守恩

translations.literal: Deng Shouen
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shouen

sentences.zh: 宋世待宦者甚嚴。

translations.literal: The Song dynasty treated eunuchs very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Song, eunuchs were kept under strict control.

sentences.zh: 太祖初定天下，掖庭給事不過五十人，宦寺中年方許養子為後。

translations.literal: When Taizu first settled the realm, inner-palace attendants numbered no more than fifty, and eunuchs were permitted to adopt heirs only in their middle years.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor Taizu first consolidated the realm, the inner palace was limited to no more than fifty attendants, and eunuchs were allowed to adopt heirs only after reaching middle age.

sentences.zh: 又詔臣僚家毋私蓄閹人，民間有閹童孺為貨鬻者論死。

translations.literal: He also decreed that ministers' households must not privately keep castrated men; anyone who sold castrated boys as merchandise was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: He further decreed that no official household might privately keep castrated servants, and that anyone who traded in castrated boys would be put to death.

sentences.zh: 去唐未遠，有所懲也。

translations.literal: The Tang was not far removed; there was something to be warned against.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang lay not far behind them, and there were hard lessons to heed.

sentences.zh: 厥後，太宗卻宰相之請，不授王繼恩宣徽；

translations.literal: Thereafter Taizong rejected the chancellor's request and did not grant Wang Jien the Xuanhui commission;
translations.idiomatic: Later, Emperor Taizong turned aside the chancellors' plea and refused to appoint Wang Jien Xuanhui Commissioner;

sentences.zh: 真宗欲以劉承規為節度使，宰相持不可而止。

translations.literal: Zhenzong wished to make Liu Chenggui a military commissioner, but the chancellors held that it was impermissible and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong wished to appoint Liu Chenggui military commissioner, but the chancellors objected that this could not be allowed, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 中更主幼母後聽政者凡三朝，在於前代，豈非宦者用事之秋乎！

translations.literal: In between there were three reigns in which young rulers and empress dowagers held court—by the standards of earlier ages, was this not the season for eunuchs to wield power!
translations.idiomatic: Between them came three reigns in which child emperors and empress dowagers ruled from behind the screen—by the measure of earlier dynasties, was this not precisely the moment when eunuchs seize power?!

sentences.zh: 祖宗之法嚴，宰相之權重，貂璫有懷奸慝，旋踵屏除，君臣相與防微杜漸之慮深矣。

translations.literal: The ancestral statutes were strict and the chancellors' authority weighty; if the eunuchs harbored wicked intent they were swiftly removed. Ruler and ministers together took deep thought to guard against small beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral code was strict and the chancellors' authority heavy; any eunuch who harbored treacherous designs was swiftly removed. Ruler and ministers alike were deeply alert to stop trouble before it could grow.

sentences.zh: 然而宣政間童貫、梁師成之禍，亦豈細哉！

translations.literal: Yet the calamity of Tong Guan and Liang Shicheng in the Xuanhe era—was that a small matter!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the disasters wrought by Tong Guan and Liang Shicheng in the Xuanhe reign—were those trifling affairs?!

sentences.zh: 南渡苗、劉之逆，亦宦者所激也。

translations.literal: The rebellion of Miao and Liu after the southward crossing was also stirred up by eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao and Liu mutiny after the court fled south was likewise provoked by eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 《坊記》曰：「君子之道，辟則坊與！

translations.literal: The "Record of the Dyke" says: "The way of the gentleman—does it not require dykes!
translations.idiomatic: The "Record of the Dyke" says: "The way of the gentleman—is it not hedged about with dykes?!

sentences.zh: 大為之坊，民猶逾之。

translations.literal: Even when great dykes are built, the people still climb over them."
translations.idiomatic: Even when great dykes are raised, the people still climb over them."

sentences.zh: 」可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Is this not a warning!
translations.idiomatic: Should this not give us pause!

sentences.zh: 作《宦者傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Biographies of Eunuchs" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biographies of Eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 竇神寶，父思儼，五代時為內侍，宋初皇城使。

translations.literal: Dou Shenbao—his father Siyan was an inner attendant in the Five Dynasties and became Director of the Imperial City at the beginning of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Shenbao was the son of Siyan, who had served as an inner attendant under the Five Dynasties and became Director of the Imperial City in the early Song.

sentences.zh: 兄神興，左領軍衛大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shenxing was a retired Grand General of the Left Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shenxing had retired as Grand General of the Left Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 神寶初為黃門，太平興國中，從征太原，擐甲登城，中流矢，稍遷入內高品，監并州戍兵。

translations.literal: Shenbao was at first a Yellow Gate attendant; in the Taiping Xingguo era he followed the campaign against Taiyuan, donned armor and climbed the walls, was struck by an arrow, and was gradually promoted to senior inner rank, supervising the garrison troops of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenbao began as a Yellow Gate attendant. During the Taiping Xingguo reign he joined the campaign against Taiyuan, put on armor and scaled the walls, took an arrow wound, and was gradually promoted within the palace ranks to oversee the Bingzhou frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 屢出襲賊，前後破砦三十六，斬千餘級，大獲鎧甲、牛馬、橐駝，因築三砦。

translations.literal: He repeatedly went out to raid the enemy, in all breaking thirty-six stockades, beheading more than a thousand, and taking great quantities of armor, cattle, horses, and camels; he then built three stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He led repeated raids against the enemy, destroying thirty-six stockades in all, killing more than a thousand men, and capturing vast stores of armor, cattle, horses, and camels; he then built three new stockades.

sentences.zh: 詔褒之。

translations.literal: An edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 九年，命與尹憲屯夏州，時岌伽羅膩等十四族久叛，神寶率兵大破之，焚其廬帳，斬千餘級，虜獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered with Yin Xian to garrison Xiazhou; at that time the fourteen tribes including Jialuoni had long been in rebellion. Shenbao led troops and routed them, burning their tents, beheading more than a thousand, and taking captives and booty in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was ordered to garrison Xiazhou with Yin Xian. The fourteen tribes including Jialuoni had long been in revolt; Shenbao led his troops to a great victory, burned their camps, killed more than a thousand men, and took captives and booty in vast numbers.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，朝廷遣使綏、宥、麟、府州，募邊部願攻契丹者，賜以金帛。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era the court sent envoys to Sui, You, Lin, and Fuzhou to recruit border tribes willing to attack the Khitan and reward them with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi reign the court sent envoys to Sui, You, Lin, and Fu prefectures to recruit border tribes willing to attack the Khitan, promising rewards of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 神寶上言：「狼子野心，由此或生邊隙。

translations.literal: Shenbao memorialized: "Wolfish hearts and savage ambitions—from this border troubles may arise.
translations.idiomatic: Shenbao memorialized: "These are wolfish hearts with savage ambitions; this may yet stir up trouble on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " The plan was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was then halted.

sentences.zh: 俄轉殿頭高品。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to senior rank in the Hall Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to senior rank in the Hall Directorate.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，使河東，閱視堡柵兵騎。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era he was sent to Hedong to inspect the troops and cavalry of the stockades and forts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua reign he was dispatched to Hedong to inspect the troops and cavalry stationed at the border forts.

sentences.zh: 慕容德豐自邢台徙延州，未至郡，詔神寶乘傳權州事。

translations.literal: Murong Defeng was transferred from Xingtai to Yanzhou; before he reached the prefecture, Shenbao was ordered to travel post-haste and act as temporary prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Defeng was transferred from Xingtai to Yanzhou, but before he could reach his post Shenbao was ordered to ride post-haste and administer the prefecture in his stead.

sentences.zh: 環州近邊內擾，與陳德玄討之，破牛家族二十八部，且規度通遠入靈武路，就命環慶同駐泊。

translations.literal: Within the borders of Huanzhou there was disturbance; with Chen Dexuan he campaigned against it, defeating twenty-eight divisions of the Niu clan, and surveyed the route from Tongyuan into Lingwu; he was then ordered to garrison jointly at Huan and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Trouble broke out along the Huanzhou frontier; with Chen Dexuan he suppressed it, defeating twenty-eight divisions of the Niu clan, and surveyed the road from Tongyuan into Lingwu. He was then ordered to establish a joint garrison at Huan and Qing.

sentences.zh: 牛家族復結眾叛，又破之，殲餘黨於極泉鎮，獲其渠帥九人。

translations.literal: The Niu clan again gathered followers and rebelled; he defeated them again, annihilating the remnant band at Jiquan town and capturing nine of their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: The Niu clan rallied and rebelled again; he defeated them once more, wiping out the remnant force at Jiquan town and capturing nine of their chieftains.

sentences.zh: 西戎寇鄜，以援之之勞，遷供奉官，與田紹斌部送靈州芻糧，即命駐泊。

translations.literal: The western Rong raided Fu; for the merit of aiding in the defense he was promoted to Palace Attendant, and with Tian Shaobin escorted fodder to Lingzhou, then was ordered to remain garrisoned there.
translations.idiomatic: When the western tribes raided Fu, he was promoted to Palace Attendant for his service in the relief effort. With Tian Shaobin he escorted fodder to Lingzhou and was ordered to remain on garrison duty there.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷入寇，與慕容德豐襲破其堡砦，焚帳幕，獲人畜數萬計。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian invaded, with Murong Defeng he raided and broke his stockades, burned the tents, and took people and livestock numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiqian invaded, he joined Murong Defeng in a raid that smashed the rebel stockades, burned their camps, and captured people and livestock by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 連詔嘉獎，遷內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Repeated edicts commended him, and he was promoted to Honored Rank of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated edicts praised his service, and he was promoted to Honored Rank of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 至道初，繼遷再寇靈武，神寶遣人間道告急闕下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao era Jiqian again raided Lingwu; Shenbao sent men by secret routes to report the emergency to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhidao reign Li Jiqian raided Lingwu again; Shenbao sent messengers by hidden routes to report the emergency to court.

sentences.zh: 賊圍之歲餘，地震二百餘日，城中糧糗皆竭，潛遣人市糴河外，宵運以入。

translations.literal: The rebels besieged the city for more than a year; earthquakes lasted more than two hundred days; grain in the city was exhausted; he secretly sent men to buy grain beyond the river and transported it in by night.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged the city for more than a year. Earthquakes shook the region for over two hundred days, and the city's grain was exhausted. He secretly sent men to buy grain beyond the river and had it carried in by night.

sentences.zh: 間出兵擊賊，賊引去，以功拜西京作坊副使。

translations.literal: From time to time he sent troops out to strike the enemy; the enemy withdrew, and for his merit he was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops out from time to time to strike the enemy, who eventually withdrew. For this service he was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.

sentences.zh: 又命於浦洛河、清遠軍援芻糧，與楊允恭議造小車三千，運糧至環州。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to transport fodder in relief at the Puluo River and Qingyuan Army; with Yang Yonggong he devised three thousand small carts to convey grain to Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to transport fodder to the Puluo River and Qingyuan Army garrisons. With Yang Yonggong he designed three thousand small carts to haul grain as far as Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷西京左藏庫副使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 出使靈武，還，奏對稱旨，面授供備庫使。

translations.literal: On a mission to Lingwu, upon his return his audience responses pleased the throne, and he was personally appointed Commissioner of the Supply Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Lingwu he returned to court and answered so well in audience that the emperor personally appointed him Commissioner of the Supply Treasury.

sentences.zh: 咸平中出為高陽關鈐轄，徙貝、冀巡檢。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he went out as Controller at Gaoyang Pass and was transferred to Inspector of Bei and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping reign he was posted as Controller at Gaoyang Pass, then transferred to frontier inspector of Bei and Ji.

sentences.zh: 會原州野狸族三千餘眾徙帳於順成穀，大蟲堪與熟魏族接戰，詔神寶和洽之，至則定其經界，遣悉還舊地。

translations.literal: It happened that more than three thousand of the Yeli tribe of Yuanzhou moved their camps to Shuncheng Valley; Dachongkan fought with the Shuwei tribe; Shenbao was ordered to reconcile them; on arrival he fixed their boundaries and sent all back to their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand members of the Yeli tribe of Yuanzhou moved their camps into Shuncheng Valley, where Dachongkan clashed with the Shuwei tribe. Shenbao was ordered to mediate; on arrival he fixed their boundaries and sent all parties back to their former lands.

sentences.zh: 入為內侍右班副都知。

translations.literal: He entered the palace as Deputy Director of the Right Division of Inner Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Deputy Director of the Right Division of Inner Attendants.

sentences.zh: 真宗朝陵，留與劉承珪同掌大內事。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong visited the imperial tombs, he was left with Liu Chenggui jointly to manage inner-palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong visited the imperial tombs, Shenbao was left behind with Liu Chenggui to manage affairs within the palace.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，勾當三班院，又掌諸王宮事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he managed the Three-Rank Bureau and also oversaw the princes' palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era he managed the Three-Rank Bureau and also oversaw affairs in the princes' palaces.

sentences.zh: 遷西京左藏庫使、領密州刺史兼掌往來國信。

translations.literal: He was promoted Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury, concurrently Prefect of Mizhou, and also managed incoming and outgoing state correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury, made concurrent prefect of Mizhou, and placed in charge of diplomatic correspondence.

sentences.zh: 神寶蒞職精恪，性吝嗇，畜貨巨萬。

translations.literal: Shenbao was meticulous and conscientious in office, but by nature stingy, amassing goods worth tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Shenbao was meticulous and conscientious in office, but by nature miserly, and he amassed wealth in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，以皇城使罷內職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi he was made Director of the Imperial City and relieved of inner duties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxi reign he was made Director of the Imperial City and relieved of his inner-palace duties.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 錄其子守志為入內供奉官。

translations.literal: His son Shouzhi was enrolled as an Inner Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouzhi was enrolled as an Inner Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 國朝以來，內侍都知、押班不領他職。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the dynasty, the Directors and Deputy Directors of Inner Attendants did not hold other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, the Directors and Deputy Directors of Inner Attendants had not held other offices.

sentences.zh: 淳化、至道後，皆內殿崇班以上兼充，多至諸司使，有領觀察使者，沒皆有贈官，官給葬事。

translations.literal: After Chunhua and Zhidao, all were concurrently filled from Honored Rank of the Inner Hall and above; many rose to commissioners of various bureaus, and some held observation commissioner posts; on death all received posthumous offices and state-provided funerals.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chunhua and Zhidao reigns these posts were filled concurrently from Honored Rank of the Inner Hall upward; many rose to head various bureaus, and some even held observation commissioner appointments. On death they all received posthumous offices and state-funded funerals.

sentences.zh: 舊制，內侍人許養一子，以充繼嗣。

translations.literal: By old regulation inner attendants were permitted to adopt one son to serve as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, inner attendants were permitted to adopt one son as heir.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，以其爭財起訟，詔自今滿三十無養父者，始聽養子，仍以其名上宣徽院，違者準前詔抵死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, because of lawsuits arising from disputes over property, an edict declared that from then on only those thirty or older without an adoptive father might adopt a son; their names were still to be reported to the Xuanhui Bureau; violators were to be punished by death as in the previous edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao, lawsuits over disputed inheritances led to a new edict: only men thirty or older who had no adoptive father might now adopt a son, and the adoption still had to be reported to the Xuanhui Bureau. Violators were still subject to death under the earlier decree.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，徐誌通為溫、台等州巡檢，坐取李歡男四人為假子，又縱卒略民家小兒，致其母抱兒投海死，決杖配掃灑班，復申前詔以戒厲之。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era Xu Zhitong was inspector of Wen, Tai, and other prefectures; he was convicted of taking four of Li Huan's sons as nominal heirs and of letting his soldiers seize small children from common households, causing one mother to drown herself with her child; he was sentenced to beating and assigned to the Sweeper Corps, and the earlier edict was proclaimed again as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping reign Xu Zhitong served as inspector of Wen, Tai, and other prefectures. He was convicted of taking four of Li Huan's sons as nominal heirs and of letting his soldiers seize children from common households, driving one mother to drown herself with her child. He was beaten with the rod and assigned to the Sweeper Corps, and the earlier edict was proclaimed again as a warning.

sentences.zh: 王繼恩，陝州陝人。

translations.literal: Wang Jien was a native of Shan in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jien was a native of Shan district in Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中為內班高品。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou he was a senior attendant of the Inner Corps.
translations.idiomatic: During the Later Zhou Xiande reign he served as a senior attendant of the Inner Corps.

sentences.zh: 初養於張氏，名德鈞。

translations.literal: He was first raised by the Zhang family and named Dejun.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been raised by the Zhang family and was known as Dejun.

sentences.zh: 開寶中求復本宗，太祖召見，許之，因賜名焉。

translations.literal: In Kaibao he petitioned to restore his original clan; Taizu summoned and received him, granted it, and bestowed his present name.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaibao era he petitioned to restore his original surname. Taizu received him in audience, granted the request, and bestowed his present name.

sentences.zh: 累為內侍行首。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to head the inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to become chief of the inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 會討江南，與竇神興等部禁兵及戰船抵采石。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Jiangnan was undertaken, with Dou Shenxing and others he led the palace troops and war vessels to Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Jiangnan was launched, he joined Dou Shenxing and others in leading the palace troops and war vessels to Caishi.

sentences.zh: 九年春，改裏面內班小底都知，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year he was made Director of the Junior Inner Corps and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he was made Director of the Junior Inner Corps and granted the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 十月，加武德使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was made Wude Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made Wude Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，副杜彥圭案行陵地，尋充永昌陵使。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, he assisted Du Yankui in surveying the tomb site and soon became Commissioner of the Yongchang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu died, he assisted Du Yankui in surveying the tomb site and soon became Commissioner of the Yongchang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，遷宮苑使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to Palace Parks Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to Palace Parks Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，領河州刺史，掌軍器弓槍庫。

translations.literal: After a long while he held the prefecture of Hezhou and managed the Arsenal of Bows and Spears.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made prefect of Hezhou and placed in charge of the Arsenal of Bows and Spears.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，王師克雲、朔，命繼恩率師屯易州，又為天雄軍駐泊都監。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era the imperial army took Yun and Shuo; Jien was ordered to lead troops garrisoned at Yizhou and was also made Chief Controller of the Tianxiong Army garrison.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi reign the imperial army captured Yun and Shuo. Jien was ordered to lead troops garrisoned at Yizhou and was also made Chief Controller of the Tianxiong Army garrison.

sentences.zh: 自岐溝關、君子館敗績之後，河朔諸路為契丹所擾，城壘多圮。

translations.literal: After the defeats at Qigou Pass and Junzi Lodge, the circuits of Heshuo were harassed by the Khitan and many walls and forts lay in ruins.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeats at Qigou Pass and Junzi Lodge, the Khitan harassed the circuits of Heshuo and many walls and forts lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔繼恩與翟守素、田仁朗、郭延濬分路按行增築之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jien was ordered with Zhai Shousu, Tian Renlang, and Guo Yanjun to tour by separate routes and rebuild and extend them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Jien was ordered, together with Zhai Shousu, Tian Renlang, and Guo Yanjun, to tour the region by separate routes and rebuild and extend the fortifications.

sentences.zh: 及遣將北伐，又為排陣都監，屯中山，改皇城使。

translations.literal: When generals were sent on the northern expedition, he was again made Chief Controller of Battle Arrays, garrisoned at Zhongshan, and transferred to Director of the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: When generals were dispatched on the northern expedition, he was again made Chief Controller of Battle Arrays, garrisoned at Zhongshan, and promoted to Director of the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，領本州團練使，又為鎮、定、高陽關三路排陣鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he held the regimental commissioner post of his native prefecture and was also Controller of Battle Arrays for the three routes of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong reign he held the regimental commissioner post of his native prefecture and was also made Controller of Battle Arrays for the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass routes.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，賜甲第一區。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was granted one first-rank residence.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua reign he was granted a first-rank residence.

sentences.zh: 五年，加昭宣使，勾當皇城司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Zhaoxuan Commissioner and managed the Imperial City Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Zhaoxuan Commissioner and placed in charge of the Imperial City Bureau.

sentences.zh: 李順亂成都，命為劍南兩川招安使，率兵討之。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled at Chengdu, Jien was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Two Shu of Jiannan and led troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled at Chengdu, Jien was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Two Shu of Jiannan and led troops to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 軍事委其制置，不從中覆。

translations.literal: Military affairs were entrusted to his disposition without requiring central review.
translations.idiomatic: Full military authority was entrusted to his discretion, without requiring approval from the capital.

sentences.zh: 管內諸州係囚，非十惡正贓，悉得以便宜決遣。

translations.literal: Prisoners held in the prefectures under his jurisdiction, unless guilty of the ten abominations or major theft, might all be disposed of at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners held in the prefectures under his jurisdiction, unless guilty of one of the ten abominations or major theft, might all be disposed of at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 二月，命馬步軍都軍頭王杲趣劍門、崇儀使尹元由峽路分遣討賊，並受繼恩節度。

translations.literal: In the second month the Commander of the Cavalry and Infantry Wang Gao was ordered to advance on Jianmen, and the Honored Ritual Envoy Yin Yuan by the Gorges route to attack the rebels by separate detachments; both were placed under Jien's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Commander of the Cavalry and Infantry Wang Gao was ordered to advance on Jianmen, while the Honored Ritual Envoy Yin Yuan was sent by the Gorges route; both operated under Jien's command.

sentences.zh: 詔前軍所至，其賊黨敢抗王師者，即須殺戮；

translations.literal: An edict declared that wherever the vanguard reached, rebel partisans who dared resist the imperial army were to be killed at once;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that wherever the vanguard reached, any rebel who dared resist the imperial army was to be killed on the spot;

sentences.zh: 如本非同惡，受制凶徒，先被脅從今能歸順者，悉釋其罪。

translations.literal: but if they had not originally shared in the crime, had been compelled by violent men, and had first been coerced but now could submit, their offenses were all to be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: but those who had not originally shared in the crime, who had been forced by the ringleaders, and who now submitted were to be pardoned entirely.

sentences.zh: 四月，繼恩由小劍門路入研石砦破賊，斬首五百級，逐北過青強嶺，平劍州，進破賊五千於柳池驛，斬千六百級，賊眾望風奔走，殺戮溺死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Jien entered by the Lesser Jianmen route, took Yanshi stockade and defeated the rebels, beheading five hundred; pursuing north past Qingqiang Ridge he pacified Jianzhou, advanced and defeated five thousand rebels at Liuchi Post, beheading sixteen hundred; the rebel masses fled at the sight of his banners, and those killed or drowned were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Jien entered by the Lesser Jianmen route, stormed Yanshi stockade, and defeated the rebels, taking five hundred heads. Pursuing north past Qingqiang Ridge he pacified Jianzhou, then routed five thousand rebels at Liuchi Post, taking sixteen hundred heads. The rebel masses fled at the sight of his banners, and the dead—killed or drowned—were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 又克閬、綿二州。

translations.literal: He also took the two prefectures of Lang and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured the prefectures of Lang and Mian.

sentences.zh: 五月，至成都，破賊十萬餘，斬首三萬級，獲順及鎧甲、僭偽服用甚眾。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he reached Chengdu, defeated more than a hundred thousand rebels, beheaded thirty thousand, and captured Shun together with vast quantities of armor and usurped regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he reached Chengdu, defeated more than a hundred thousand rebels, took thirty thousand heads, and captured Li Shun along with vast stores of armor and usurped regalia.

sentences.zh: 朝議賞功，中書欲除宣徽使。

translations.literal: The court debated rewarding his merit; the Secretariat wished to appoint him Xuanhui Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated how to reward him; the Secretariat proposed appointing him Xuanhui Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「朕讀前代史書，不欲令宦官預政事。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "I have read the histories of former ages and do not wish eunuchs to participate in government.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "I have read the histories of former ages and do not wish eunuchs to take part in government.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使，執政之漸也，止可授以他官。

translations.literal: The Xuanhui Commissioner is a step toward holding power; he may be granted only some other office."
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanhui Commissioner is a step toward wielding power; grant him some other office instead."

sentences.zh: 」宰相力言繼恩有大功，非此任無足以為賞典。

translations.literal: The chancellors strongly argued that Jien had great merit and that no other appointment would suffice as reward.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors insisted that Jien's merit was so great that no lesser appointment would suffice as reward.

sentences.zh: 上怒，深責相臣，命學士張洎、錢若水議別立宣政使，序位昭宣使上以授之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sharply rebuked the ministers, ordering Academicians Zhang Ji and Qian Ruoshui to devise a separate office of Xuanzheng Commissioner ranked above the Zhaoxuan Commissioner, and this was granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and sharply rebuked his ministers. He ordered Academicians Zhang Ji and Qian Ruoshui to devise a new office of Xuanzheng Commissioner, ranked above the Zhaoxuan Commissioner, and granted that title to Jien instead.

sentences.zh: 進領順州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was further made Defense Commissioner of Shunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Defense Commissioner of Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 繼恩握重兵，久留成都，轉餉不給，專以宴飲為務。

translations.literal: Jien held heavy forces and remained long at Chengdu; supplies could not be forwarded, and he devoted himself solely to feasting and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Jien held a large army and lingered long at Chengdu. Supplies could not keep up, and he devoted himself chiefly to feasting and drinking.

sentences.zh: 每出入，前後奏音樂。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out or in, music was played before and behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad, musicians played before and behind him.

sentences.zh: 又令騎兵執博局棋枰自隨，威振郡縣。

translations.literal: He also ordered cavalry to carry gambling boards and chess sets with them; his authority awed prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: He even had his cavalry carry gambling boards and chess sets wherever they went, and his authority awed every prefecture and district.

sentences.zh: 仆使輩用事恣橫，縱所部剽掠子女金帛，軍士亦無鬥志。

translations.literal: His servants and attendants wielded power wantonly, letting their men plunder women, children, gold, and silk; the soldiers too lost fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His servants and attendants wielded power wantonly, letting their men plunder women, children, gold, and silk, and the soldiers lost all fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 餘賊迸伏山谷間，州縣有復陷者。

translations.literal: Remnant rebels scattered and hid in the valleys; some prefectures and districts were lost again.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant rebels scattered into the mountain valleys, and some prefectures and districts fell again.

sentences.zh: 太宗知之，乃命入內押班衛紹欽同領其事。

translations.literal: When Taizong learned of this, he ordered the Inner Deputy Director Wei Shaoqin to share command of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong learned of this, he ordered the Inner Deputy Director Wei Shaoqin to share command of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 又遣樞密直學士張鑒、西京作坊副使馮守規乘傳督其捕賊。

translations.literal: He also sent Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Jian and Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops Feng Shougui post-haste to supervise the capture of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Jian and Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops Feng Shougui post-haste to supervise the hunt for the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 議分減師徒出蜀境，以便糧運。

translations.literal: It was proposed to reduce the army in stages and withdraw from Shu territory to ease the transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated reducing the army in stages and withdrawing from Shu territory to ease the transport of provisions.

sentences.zh: 高品王文壽者，隸繼恩麾下，繼恩遣領虎翼卒二千，分遂州路追討。

translations.literal: There was a senior attendant Wang Wenshou who served under Jien; Jien sent him to lead two thousand Tiger-Wing troops to pursue the rebels along the Suizhou route.
translations.idiomatic: A senior attendant named Wang Wenshou served under Jien, who sent him with two thousand Tiger-Wing troops to pursue the rebels along the Suizhou route.

sentences.zh: 文壽禦下嚴急，士卒皆怨。

translations.literal: Wenshou governed his men with harsh severity, and the soldiers all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshou ruled his men with harsh severity, and the soldiers resented him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 一夕臥帳中，指揮使張嶙遣卒排闥入，斬文壽首以出。

translations.literal: One night as he lay in his tent, the commander Zhang Lin sent soldiers to burst in, beheaded Wenshou, and carried the head out.
translations.idiomatic: One night as he lay in his tent, Commander Zhang Lin sent soldiers to burst in, beheaded Wenshou, and carried out his head.

sentences.zh: 會夜昏黑，嶙猶疑其非，然炬照之，曰：「是也。

translations.literal: The night was dark, and Lin still doubted it was really he; he lit a torch to look and said, "It is he.
translations.idiomatic: The night was dark, and Lin still doubted the head was genuine; he lit a torch to look and said, "It is he.

sentences.zh: 」時嘉州賊帥張餘有眾萬餘，嶙即以所部與之合，賊勢甚盛。

translations.literal: " At that time the rebel chief Zhang Yu of Jiazhou had more than ten thousand followers; Lin joined his force with them, and the rebels grew very strong.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the rebel chief Zhang Yu of Jiazhou commanded more than ten thousand men. Lin joined his troops with the rebels, and their strength grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 初奏至，太宗欲盡誅軍人妻子，近臣或請勿殺，悉索營中書，遣帥招撫，諭以釋罪，親屬皆全，必自引來歸，因可破賊。

translations.literal: When the first report arrived, Taizong wished to execute all the soldiers' wives and children; some close ministers urged that they not be killed, that all writings in the camps be gathered, and that commanders be sent to offer pacification, announcing pardon so that families would be spared and the men would surely come back of themselves, thereby breaking the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the first report reached court, Taizong wished to execute all the soldiers' wives and children. Some close ministers urged mercy: gather the writings left in the camps, send commanders to offer pacification, and announce a pardon so that families would be spared and the men would return of their own accord—thus breaking the rebels.

sentences.zh: 上然之，令巡檢程道符諭旨。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and ordered the inspector Cheng Daofu to proclaim the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered Inspector Cheng Daofu to proclaim the edict.

sentences.zh: 亡卒斬嶙，函首送繼恩，皆自拔來歸。

translations.literal: The fugitive soldiers killed Lin, sent his head in a box to Jien, and all came forward to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitive soldiers killed Lin, sent his head in a box to Jien, and all came forward to surrender.

sentences.zh: 因使為鄉導擊賊，悉平之。

translations.literal: They were then made local guides to attack the rebels, and all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They were then employed as local guides to hunt down the rebels, and all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 至道二年春，布衣韓拱辰詣闕上言：「繼恩有平賊大功，當秉機務，今止得防禦使，賞甚薄，無以慰中外之望。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Zhidao, the commoner Han Gongchen came to court and memorialized: "Jien has great merit in pacifying the rebels and ought to hold state affairs; now he receives only a defense commissioner post—the reward is very thin and cannot satisfy the hopes of court and realm."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Zhidao, a commoner named Han Gongchen came to court and memorialized: "Jien earned great merit in pacifying the rebels and ought to hold state affairs; yet he receives only a defense commissioner post—a reward too thin to satisfy the hopes of court and realm."

sentences.zh: 」上大怒，以拱辰惑眾，杖脊黥面配崖州。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, deemed Gongchen a demagogue, had his back beaten and his face tattooed, and exiled him to Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. He deemed Gongchen a demagogue, had his back beaten and his face tattooed, and exiled him to Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 俄召繼恩。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Jien was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Jien was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，命與李神福按行山陵，加領桂州觀察使。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, he was ordered with Li Shenfu to survey the mausoleum site and was additionally made Observation Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, he was ordered with Li Shenfu to survey the mausoleum site and was additionally made Observation Commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 繼恩初事太祖，特承恩顧。

translations.literal: Jien had first served Taizu and received his special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jien had first served Taizu and enjoyed his special favor.

sentences.zh: 及崩夕，太宗在南府，繼恩中夜馳詣府邸，請太宗入，太宗忠之，自是寵遇莫比。

translations.literal: On the night of Taizu's death, Taizong was at the Southern Residence; Jien rode post-haste in the middle of the night to the residence and urged Taizong to enter. Taizong was grateful, and from then on no one matched his favor.
translations.idiomatic: On the night Taizu died, Taizong was at the Southern Residence. Jien rode post-haste in the dead of night to the residence and urged Taizong to enter. Taizong never forgot this loyalty, and from then on no one matched his favor.

sentences.zh: 喜結黨邀名譽，乘間或敢言薦外朝臣，由是士大夫之輕薄好進者從之交往，每以多寶院僧舍為期。

translations.literal: He delighted in forming factions to win reputation and, seizing opportunities, sometimes dared recommend outer-court officials; thus frivolous, ambitious literati associated with him, often meeting at the Duobao Cloister.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in forming factions to win reputation and sometimes dared recommend outer-court officials when chance offered. Frivolous, ambitious literati flocked to him, often meeting at the Duobao Cloister.

sentences.zh: 有潘閬者能詩詠，賣藥京師，繼恩薦之，召見，賜進士第。

translations.literal: There was a Pan Lang skilled in poetry who sold medicine in the capital; Jien recommended him, he was summoned and granted the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Pan Lang skilled in poetry who sold medicine in the capital. Jien recommended him; he was summoned to court and granted the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 尋察其狂妄，追還詔書。

translations.literal: Soon his arrogance was discovered and the edict was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his arrogance was discovered and the imperial edict was recalled.

sentences.zh: 及真宗初，繼恩益豪橫，頗欺罔，漏泄機事，與參知政事李昌齡緘題往來，多請托，至有連宮禁者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong's reign Jien grew still more overbearing, deceived frequently, and leaked state secrets; he exchanged sealed letters with Vice Grand Councilor Li Changling, making many requests, some even touching the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenzong's reign Jien grew still more overbearing, deceived frequently, and leaked state secrets. He exchanged sealed letters with Vice Grand Councilor Li Changling, making many requests, some even touching the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 素與胡旦善，時將加恩，密諉其為褒辭。

translations.literal: He had long been friendly with Hu Dan; when honors were about to be granted, he secretly asked him to compose laudatory words.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Hu Dan. When honors were about to be granted, he secretly asked him to compose laudatory words.

sentences.zh: 又士人詩頌盈門。

translations.literal: Moreover, literati's poems of praise filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Literati's poems of praise filled his gate.

sentences.zh: 上惡其朋結，黜為右監門衛將軍、均州安置，籍沒貲產，多得蜀土僭擬之物。

translations.literal: The emperor detested his faction-making, demoted him to General of the Right Gate Guard, and exiled him to Junzhou; his property was confiscated, and much of it consisted of usurped regalia from Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor detested his faction-making, demoted him to General of the Right Gate Guard, and exiled him to Junzhou. His property was confiscated, and much of it consisted of usurped regalia from Shu.

sentences.zh: 昌齡責忠武軍節度行軍司馬，旦削籍，長流尋州。

translations.literal: Changling was demoted to campaigning marshal of the Zhongwu Army; Dan was struck from the rolls and exiled far to Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Changling was demoted to campaigning marshal of the Zhongwu Army; Dan was struck from the rolls and exiled far to Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔中外臣僚曾與繼恩交識及通書尺者，一切不問。

translations.literal: An edict declared that all inner and outer officials who had known Jien or exchanged letters with him would not be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that all officials who had known Jien or exchanged letters with him would not be questioned.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，卒於貶所，遣使將其家屬還京師，假官舍處之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he died at his place of exile; envoys were sent to bring his family back to the capital and lodge them in a government residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he died in exile. Envoys were sent to bring his family back to the capital and lodge them in a government residence.

sentences.zh: 四年，聽歸葬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was permitted to be buried at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was permitted burial in his home district.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，特詔追復官爵，以白金千兩賜其家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu a special edict restored his offices and titles, and a thousand taels of white silver were granted to his family.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu a special edict restored his offices and titles, and a thousand taels of white silver were granted to his family.

sentences.zh: 子懷珪，轉入內高班。

translations.literal: His son Huaigui was transferred into the senior inner corps.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaigui was transferred into the senior inner corps.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷皇城使、內侍省入內內侍都知，領恩州團練使、勾當永熙陵行宮事。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, Shenfu was made Director of the Imperial City and Director of Inner Attendants of the Inner Service, concurrently Regimental Commissioner of Enzhou and manager of the Yongxi Mausoleum traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded, Shenfu was made Director of the Imperial City and Director of Inner Attendants of the Inner Service, concurrently Regimental Commissioner of Enzhou and manager of the Yongxi Mausoleum traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 時模寫太宗聖容，以神福立侍。

translations.literal: At that time a portrait of Taizong's sacred likeness was being copied, with Shenfu standing in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a portrait of Taizong's sacred likeness was being painted, with Shenfu standing in attendance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，求罷都知，加昭宣使、勾當皇城司，賜第宮城側，遣修內工為葺之。

translations.literal: Before long he asked to be relieved of the directorship, was made Zhaoxuan Commissioner and manager of the Imperial City Bureau, granted a residence beside the palace, and palace artisans were sent to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to be relieved of the directorship, was made Zhaoxuan Commissioner and placed in charge of the Imperial City Bureau, and was granted a residence beside the palace, which palace artisans were sent to repair.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年秋，閱兵東郊，以神福為大內都部署。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Xianping, when troops were reviewed at the Eastern Suburb, Shenfu was made Chief Deployer of the Great Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Xianping, when troops were reviewed at the Eastern Suburb, Shenfu was made Chief Deployer of the Great Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 是冬，幸大名，與王繼英並為行宮使。

translations.literal: That winter, when the emperor visited Daming, he and Wang Jiying were both made traveling palace commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the emperor visited Daming, he and Wang Jiying were both made traveling palace commissioners.

sentences.zh: 四年，勾當三班，部修含光殿，賜賚甚優。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he managed the Three-Rank Bureau and supervised repair of the Hanguang Hall; the gifts granted were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he managed the Three-Rank Bureau and supervised repair of the Hanguang Hall; the gifts granted him were very generous.

sentences.zh: 景德初，兼領親王諸宮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he also held the post of commissioner of the princes' palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde reign he also held the post of commissioner of the princes' palaces.

sentences.zh: 三年，改宣政使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Xuanzheng Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Xuanzheng Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從謁諸陵，復為行宮使。

translations.literal: Accompanying visits to the imperial tombs, he again served as traveling palace commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying visits to the imperial tombs, he again served as traveling palace commissioner.

sentences.zh: 進幸西京，賜酺，命神福主其事。

translations.literal: When the emperor advanced to the Western Capital and granted a public feast, Shenfu was ordered to preside over it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor advanced to the Western Capital and granted a public feast, Shenfu was ordered to preside over it.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，天書降夕，神福與劉承珪、鄧永遷、李神祐、石知顒、張景宗、藍繼宗同直禁中，賜以器幣、緡錢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, on the night the Heavenly Writ descended, Shenfu with Liu Chenggui, Deng Yongqian, Li Shenyou, Shi Zhiyong, Zhang Jingzong, and Lan Jizong kept watch together in the forbidden precinct and were granted vessels, silks, and cash.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu reign, on the night the Heavenly Writ descended, Shenfu kept watch in the forbidden precinct with Liu Chenggui, Deng Yongqian, Li Shenyou, Shi Zhiyong, Zhang Jingzong, and Lan Jizong, and they were granted vessels, silks, and cash.

sentences.zh: 京師酺會，又令神福與白文肇、閻承翰同典之。

translations.literal: For the capital feast he was again ordered with Bai Wenzhao and Yan Chenghan to direct it.
translations.idiomatic: For the capital feast he was again ordered, together with Bai Wenzhao and Yan Chenghan, to direct the ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 是歲封泰山，與曹利用同經度行宮道路。

translations.literal: That year, for the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai, he with Cao Liyong planned the traveling palace routes together.
translations.idiomatic: That year, for the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai, he and Cao Liyong planned the traveling palace routes together.

sentences.zh: 及車駕進發，又為行宮使。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage set out, he again served as traveling palace commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession set out, he again served as traveling palace commissioner.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，授宣慶使，領昭州防禦使，整肅禁衛。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was made Xuanqing Commissioner, concurrently Defense Commissioner of Shaozhou, and put the palace guard in order.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed he was made Xuanqing Commissioner, concurrently Defense Commissioner of Shaozhou, and charged with putting the palace guard in order.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸司使止於宣政，故特置使額以寵之。

translations.literal: Previously bureau commissioners stopped at Xuanzheng; therefore a separate commission was specially created to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Previously bureau commissioners had ranked no higher than Xuanzheng Commissioner; a separate title was therefore created specially to honor him.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈潤州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Observation Commissioner of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Observation Commissioner of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 神福性恭願和易，每為衛紹欽所詬罵，皆引避不校。

translations.literal: Shenfu was by nature respectful, compliant, and easygoing; whenever Wei Shaoqin reviled him he would withdraw and not contend.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu was by nature respectful, compliant, and easygoing. Whenever Wei Shaoqin reviled him he would withdraw and not contend.

sentences.zh: 在禁闥五十年，稱為長者。

translations.literal: He spent fifty years within the forbidden gates and was called an elder.
translations.idiomatic: He spent fifty years within the forbidden gates and was known as an elder.

sentences.zh: 然久掌三班，無規制，遠近失敘，有請托者不能拒之，人譏其所守。

translations.literal: Yet having long managed the Three-Rank Bureau, he kept no regulations; near and far lost proper order; when petitioners came he could not refuse them, and people mocked his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet having long managed the Three-Rank Bureau, he kept no proper regulations; appointments lost their proper order; when petitioners came he could not refuse them, and people mocked his integrity.

sentences.zh: 子懷斌、懷贇。

translations.literal: His sons were Huaibin and Huaiyun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Huaibin and Huaiyun.

sentences.zh: 弟神祐。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Shenyou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Shenyou.

sentences.zh: 神祐，初以父任授殿頭高品。

translations.literal: Shenyou—at first through his father's position he was granted senior rank in the Hall Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou first received senior rank in the Hall Directorate through his father's position.

sentences.zh: 太祖將納孝章皇后，命神祐奉聘禮於華州。

translations.literal: When Taizu was to take Empress Xiaozhang, Shenyou was ordered to present the betrothal gifts at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was to take Empress Xiaozhang as consort, Shenyou was ordered to present the betrothal gifts at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，征太原，負禦寶從行。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande, on the campaign against Taiyuan, he bore the imperial seals and accompanied the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiande, on the campaign against Taiyuan, he bore the imperial seals and accompanied the expedition.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，又從征太原，時有詔緣邊和市軍儲，車駕在潞州聞之，且慮擾民，令神祐馳驛止之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he again followed the campaign against Taiyuan; at that time an edict ordered border markets to supply military stores; the emperor at Luzhou heard of it and, fearing harm to the people, ordered Shenyou to ride post-haste and halt it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he again joined the campaign against Taiyuan. An edict had ordered border markets to supply military stores; the emperor at Luzhou heard of it and, fearing harm to the people, ordered Shenyou to ride post-haste and halt the order.

sentences.zh: 時詔下已五日，神祐一夕而及晉陽。

translations.literal: The edict had been issued five days earlier; Shenyou reached Jinyang in a single night.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had been issued five days earlier; Shenyou reached Jinyang in a single night.

sentences.zh: 一日，甲士既陣，賊潛縱火焚梯衝，亟命神祐部衛兵為援，斬賊甚眾，餘悉潰去。

translations.literal: One day, after the armored troops had formed ranks, the enemy secretly set fire to the scaling ladders and rams; Shenyou was urgently ordered to lead palace guards as reinforcements, beheaded many of the enemy, and the rest all fled.
translations.idiomatic: One day, after the armored troops had formed ranks, the enemy secretly set fire to the scaling ladders and rams. Shenyou was urgently ordered to lead palace guards as reinforcements; he killed many of the enemy and the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 王師伐廣州，隨軍賞給。

translations.literal: When the imperial army attacked Guangzhou, he accompanied it to distribute rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army attacked Guangzhou, he accompanied it to distribute rewards.

sentences.zh: 劉鋹平，先部帑藏之物赴京師。

translations.literal: When Liu Chang was pacified, he was first to escort the treasury goods to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chang was pacified, he was first to escort the treasury goods to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及土寇周瓊等叛，又副尹崇珂討平之。

translations.literal: When the local bandits Zhou Qiong and others rebelled, he again assisted Yin Chongke in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: When the local bandits Zhou Qiong and others rebelled, he again assisted Yin Chongke in suppressing them.

sentences.zh: 六年，隨曹彬南征。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Cao Bin on the southern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Cao Bin on the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 克關城，擒偽將朱令贇，命神祐馳入獻捷書，賜錦袍、金帶。

translations.literal: When Guan city was taken and the rebel general Zhu Lingyun captured, Shenyou was ordered to ride in with the victory report and was granted a brocade robe and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan city was taken and the rebel general Zhu Lingyun captured, Shenyou was ordered to ride in with the victory report and was granted a brocade robe and gold belt.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，轉內園使、邠州都監。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded, he was transferred to Inner Gardens Commissioner and Chief Controller of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded, he was transferred to Inner Gardens Commissioner and Chief Controller of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，改天雄軍都監、子城內巡檢。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured the north, he was made Chief Controller of the Tianxiong Army and inner inspector of the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the north, he was made Chief Controller of the Tianxiong Army and inner inspector of the inner city.

sentences.zh: 時北兵充斥，道途阻塞，命神祐單騎諭密旨於諸將。

translations.literal: Northern troops filled the region and the roads were blocked; Shenyou was ordered to ride alone and convey secret orders to the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops filled the region and the roads were blocked. Shenyou was ordered to ride alone and convey secret orders to the generals.

sentences.zh: 敵騎數百忽至，神祐乃周麾而呼，若召伏兵，敵懼而逃，遂達其命。

translations.literal: Several hundred enemy horsemen suddenly appeared; Shenyou wheeled his banner and shouted as if summoning hidden troops; the enemy fled in fear, and he delivered his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred enemy horsemen suddenly appeared. Shenyou wheeled his banner and shouted as if summoning hidden troops; the enemy fled in fear, and he delivered his orders.

sentences.zh: 俄充邢州排陣都監，勾當西八作司。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he served as Chief Controller of Battle Arrays at Xingzhou and managed the Western Eight Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he served as Chief Controller of Battle Arrays at Xingzhou and managed the Western Eight Workshops.

sentences.zh: 景德初，上幸澶州，領隨駕壕砦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, when the emperor visited Chanzhou, he led the entrenchments accompanying the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde reign, when the emperor visited Chanzhou, he led the entrenchments accompanying the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷入內都知。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Inner Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Inner Director.

sentences.zh: 從東封還，遷南作坊使。

translations.literal: Returning from the eastern Fengshan rites, he was made Commissioner of the Southern Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the eastern Fengshan rites, he was made Commissioner of the Southern Workshops.

sentences.zh: 時內侍將遷秩，有扈從升山、不升山或不預從祀者，令神祐第其勤狀，上親閱而敘遷之。

translations.literal: At that time inner attendants were to be promoted in rank; those who had or had not ascended the mountain in attendance, or had not joined the sacrifice, were ordered ranked by Shenyou according to their merit records; the emperor personally reviewed and ordered their promotions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time inner attendants were to be promoted in rank. Shenyou was ordered to rank them according to merit—distinguishing those who had ascended the mountain in attendance from those who had not—and the emperor personally reviewed the list and ordered their promotions.

sentences.zh: 有範守遜、皇甫文、史崇貴、張延訓等，皆嘗有譴累而互陳勞效，且言神祐等品第非當，泣訴於上，止而復來者數四。

translations.literal: Fan Shouxun, Huangfu Wen, Shi Chonggui, Zhang Yanxun, and others had all once been punished; they mutually cited their labors and said Shenyou's rankings were improper, weeping and appealing to the emperor, leaving and returning three or four times.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shouxun, Huangfu Wen, Shi Chonggui, Zhang Yanxun, and others had all once been punished. They cited one another's labors and protested that Shenyou's rankings were improper, weeping and appealing to the emperor again and again.

sentences.zh: 守遜等先改內常侍，上怒，悉停其官。

translations.literal: Shouxun and the others had first been made Inner Regular Attendants; the emperor was angry and halted all their appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxun and the others had first been made Inner Regular Attendants; the emperor was angry and halted all their appointments.

sentences.zh: 神祐洎石知顒、副都知張景宗、藍繼宗並坐削職。

translations.literal: Shenyou together with Shi Zhiyong, Deputy Director Zhang Jingzong, and Lan Jizong were all punished by reduction of office.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou, together with Shi Zhiyong, Deputy Director Zhang Jingzong, and Lan Jizong, were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 尋掌禦廚七年，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he managed the Imperial Kitchen for seven years, then died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he managed the Imperial Kitchen for seven years, then died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符六年，錄其孫永和為三班奉職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his grandson Yonghe was enrolled as a Three-Rank Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his grandson Yonghe was enrolled as a Three-Rank Attendant.

sentences.zh: 神祐性謹願，曉音律，頗好篇詠。

translations.literal: Shenyou was by nature cautious and compliant, understood music, and was fond of composing verse.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou was by nature cautious and compliant, understood music, and was fond of composing verse.

sentences.zh: 子懷岊，太宗時嘗請為道士，後復內侍。

translations.literal: His son Huaijie, in Taizong's time, once asked to become a Daoist priest, then later returned to inner service.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaijie, in Taizong's time, once asked to become a Daoist priest, then later returned to inner service.

sentences.zh: 多屯邊郡，常持大鐵鞭以鬥賊，屢中流矢，至供奉官。

translations.literal: He was often garrisoned in border prefectures, regularly wielded a great iron whip in fighting bandits, was repeatedly struck by arrows, and rose to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was often garrisoned in border prefectures, regularly wielded a great iron whip against bandits, took arrow wounds repeatedly, and rose to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 懷儼為內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Huaiyan was Honored Rank of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyan held Honored Rank of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 真宗立，瑩為宣徽使，以承規領勝州刺史、簽書宣徽院公事。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, Ying was Xuanhui Commissioner; Chenggui was made Prefect of Shengzhou and put in charge of signing Xuanhui Bureau business.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded, Ying was Xuanhui Commissioner; Chenggui was made prefect of Shengzhou and charged with signing Xuanhui Bureau business.

sentences.zh: 尋讓宣徽之務，加莊宅使。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he yielded the Xuanhui duties and was made Estates Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he yielded the Xuanhui duties and was made Estates Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，遷北作坊使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he was transferred to Commissioner of the Northern Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he was transferred to Commissioner of the Northern Workshops.

sentences.zh: 時邊境未寧，議修天雄軍城壘，命承規乘傳經畫，又命提舉內東、崇政殿等諸門，遷宮苑使。

translations.literal: The frontier was not yet settled; repair of the Tianxiong Army walls and forts was debated, and Chenggui was ordered to travel post-haste to plan it; he was also ordered to supervise the Inner East Gate, Chongzheng Hall, and other gates, and was transferred to Palace Parks Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was not yet settled. When repair of the Tianxiong Army walls and forts was debated, Chenggui was ordered to travel post-haste to plan the work. He was also ordered to supervise the Inner East Gate, Chongzheng Hall, and other gates, and was transferred to Palace Parks Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上詢承規西事，請益環州木波鎮戍兵，以為諸路之援，從之。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Chenggui about western affairs; he requested increased garrison troops at Mubo town in Huanzhou as support for the various routes, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Chenggui about western affairs. He requested increased garrison troops at Mubo town in Huanzhou as support for the various routes, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 俄兼勾當群牧司。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he also managed the Herds Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he also managed the Herds Directorate.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，與李允則使河間，按視嘗經戰陣等處將卒之勞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, with Li Yunze he was sent to Hejian to inspect the merits of officers and soldiers who had fought in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde he was sent to Hejian with Li Yunze to inspect the merits of officers and soldiers who had fought in battle.

sentences.zh: 是歲，置官提舉京師諸司庫務，以承規領之。

translations.literal: That year an office was created to supervise the capital's bureau storehouses, with Chenggui at its head.
translations.idiomatic: That year an office was created to supervise the capital's bureau storehouses, with Chenggui at its head.

sentences.zh: 所創局署，多所規制。

translations.literal: The agencies he created had many regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The agencies he created introduced many new regulations.

sentences.zh: 改皇城使。

translations.literal: He was made Director of the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 與林特、李溥議更茶法。

translations.literal: With Lin Te and Li Pu he discussed reform of the tea law.
translations.idiomatic: With Lin Te and Li Pu he discussed reform of the tea law.

sentences.zh: 四年，三司上言新課增羨，承規以勞加領昭州團練使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Three Departments reported that the new levy had increased revenue; for his labor Chenggui was additionally made Regimental Commissioner of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Three Departments reported that the new levy had increased revenue; for his service Chenggui was additionally made Regimental Commissioner of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，議封泰山，以掌發運使遷昭宣使、長州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, when Fengshan at Mount Tai was debated, as Commissioner of Transport he was promoted to Zhaoxuan Commissioner and Defense Commissioner of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu reign, when Fengshan at Mount Tai was debated, he was promoted from Commissioner of Transport to Zhaoxuan Commissioner and Defense Commissioner of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 會修玉清昭應宮，以承規為副使。

translations.literal: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace was being built, Chenggui was made deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace was being built, Chenggui was made deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，復命督運。

translations.literal: For the sacrifice at Fenyin he was again ordered to supervise transport.
translations.idiomatic: For the sacrifice at Fenyin he was again ordered to supervise transport.

sentences.zh: 議者以自京至河中，由陸則山險，具舟則湍悍，承規決議水運，凡百供應，悉安流而達。

translations.literal: Advisers held that from the capital to Hezhong, going by land meant dangerous mountains and preparing boats meant fierce currents; Chenggui decided on water transport, and all supplies reached their destination by smooth flow.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers held that from the capital to Hezhong, travel by land meant dangerous mountains and travel by boat meant fierce currents. Chenggui decided on water transport, and all supplies reached their destination safely downstream.

sentences.zh: 自朝陵、東封及是皆留掌大內。

translations.literal: From the tomb visits, the eastern Fengshan, and this occasion onward he was always left to manage the great inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: From the tomb visits, the eastern Fengshan, and this occasion onward he was always left to manage affairs within the great inner palace.

sentences.zh: 禮成，當進秩，表求休致，手詔敦勉，仍作七言詩賜之。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was due for promotion; he memorialized requesting retirement; the emperor personally wrote an edict urging him to continue, and also composed a seven-character poem as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed he was due for promotion, but he memorialized requesting retirement. The emperor personally wrote an edict urging him to continue, and also composed a seven-character poem as a gift.

sentences.zh: 拜宣政使、應州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Xuanzheng Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Xuanzheng Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，以疾求致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on account of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he requested retirement on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 修宮使丁謂言承規領宮職，藉其督轄，望勿許所請，第優賜告詔，特置景福殿使名以寵之，班在客省使上。

translations.literal: Palace Construction Commissioner Ding Wei said Chenggui held palace duties and the court relied on his supervision; he hoped the request would not be granted—only generously grant leave edicts, specially create the title Jingfu Hall Commissioner to honor him, with rank above the Guest Reception Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Construction Commissioner Ding Wei argued that Chenggui still held palace duties and that the court relied on his supervision. He urged that the request not be granted, that Chenggui be generously granted leave edicts instead, and that the special title of Jingfu Hall Commissioner be created to honor him, with rank above the Guest Reception Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 仍改新州觀察使，上作歌以賜。

translations.literal: He was also changed to Observation Commissioner of Xinzhou; the emperor composed a song as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Observation Commissioner of Xinzhou, and the emperor composed a song as a gift.

sentences.zh: 承規以廉使月稟歸於有司，手詔褒美，復定殿使奉以給之。

translations.literal: Chenggui returned the monthly salary of the inspection commissioner to the relevant office; the emperor personally wrote an edict praising him, and again fixed the Jingfu Hall Commissioner's stipend to provide for him.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui returned his monthly salary as inspection commissioner to the relevant office. The emperor personally wrote an edict praising him and again fixed the Jingfu Hall Commissioner's stipend to provide for him.

sentences.zh: 本名承珪，以久疾羸瘵，上為取道家易名度厄之義，改珪為規。

translations.literal: His original name was Chenggui; because of long illness and wasting disease, the emperor took the Daoist meaning of changing one's name to escape calamity and changed the character of his name from gui (jade tablet) to gui (compass).
translations.idiomatic: His original name had been Chenggui. Because prolonged illness had left him emaciated, the emperor invoked the Daoist practice of changing one's name to ward off disaster and altered the written form of his name.

sentences.zh: 疾甚，請解務還私第，聽之。

translations.literal: His illness was severe; he requested to leave his duties and return to his private residence; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His illness was severe. He asked to leave his duties and return to his private residence, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 仍許皇城常務上印日，內藏庫有創製，就取商度。

translations.literal: It was also permitted that on days when routine duties of the Imperial City were stamped and submitted, if the Inner Storehouse had new creations, he could be consulted at once.
translations.idiomatic: He was also allowed, on days when routine Imperial City business was formally submitted, to be consulted at once whenever the Inner Storehouse had new creations to review.

sentences.zh: 又再表求罷，官檢校太傅、左騎衛上將軍、安遠軍節度觀察留後致仕。

translations.literal: He again memorialized requesting dismissal; his titles as Acting Grand Preceptor, Senior General of the Left Horse Guard, and Military Commissioner and Observation Remainder of the Anyuan Army were let go in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again requesting dismissal. He retired from his titles as Acting Grand Preceptor, Senior General of the Left Horse Guard, and Military Commissioner and Observation Remainder of the Anyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 七月卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he died, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈左衛上將軍、鎮江軍節度，諡曰忠肅。

translations.literal: Court was suspended; he was posthumously granted Senior General of the Left Guard and Military Commissioner of the Zhenjiang Army; his posthumous title was Zhongsu (Loyal and Stern).
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences were suspended. He was posthumously granted Senior General of the Left Guard and Military Commissioner of the Zhenjiang Army, with the posthumous title Zhongsu (Loyal and Stern).

sentences.zh: 承規事三朝，以精力聞，樂較簿領，孜孜無倦。

translations.literal: Chenggui served three reigns, was known for his energy, delighted in comparing ledger accounts, and worked tirelessly without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui served three reigns and was known for his tireless energy. He delighted in auditing ledger accounts and worked diligently without ever slackening.

sentences.zh: 自掌內藏僅三十年，檢察精密，動著條式。

translations.literal: From managing the Inner Storehouse for nearly thirty years, his inspections were precise and meticulous, and his actions always conformed to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He managed the Inner Storehouse for nearly thirty years. His inspections were precise and meticulous, and his actions always conformed to established regulations.

sentences.zh: 又製定權衡法，語在《律曆志》。

translations.literal: He also formulated the Weights and Measures Law; the account is in the "Treatise on Calendars and Measures."
translations.idiomatic: He also formulated the Weights and Measures Law; the account appears in the "Treatise on Calendars and Measures."

sentences.zh: 性沈毅徇公，深所倚信，尤好伺察，人多畏之。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep and resolute, devoted to public duty, deeply trusted; he especially liked to investigate and observe, and many feared him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was grave, resolute, and devoted to public duty. The emperor trusted him deeply. He especially liked to investigate and observe, and many feared him.

sentences.zh: 上崇瑞命，修祠祀，飾宮觀，承規悉預聞。

translations.literal: The emperor honored auspicious decrees, built shrines, and decorated palaces and temples; Chenggui was fully involved in all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored auspicious heavenly mandates, built shrines, and decorated palaces and temples, and Chenggui was fully involved in all of these.

sentences.zh: 作玉清昭應宮，尤為精麗。

translations.literal: In building the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace, it was especially exquisite and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuqing Zhaoying Palace he built was especially exquisite and splendid.

sentences.zh: 屋室有少不中程，雖金碧已具，必毀而更造，有司不敢計所費。

translations.literal: If any building fell even slightly short of specifications, though gold and azure ornament were already in place, he would surely destroy it and rebuild; the officials dared not tally the cost.
translations.idiomatic: If any building fell even slightly short of specifications, he would destroy it and rebuild even when gold and azure ornament were already in place; the officials dared not tally the cost.

sentences.zh: 二聖殿塑配饗功臣，特詔塑其像太宗之側。

translations.literal: In the Hall of the Two Sages, statues of meritorious ministers were molded for the accompanying sacrifice; a special edict ordered his image molded beside Taizong's.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hall of the Two Sages, where statues of meritorious ministers were molded for the accompanying sacrifice, a special edict ordered his image placed beside Taizong's.

sentences.zh: 承規遇事亦或寬恕，鑄錢工常訴本監前後盜銅瘞地數千斤，承規佯為不納，因密遣人發取還官，不問其罪。

translations.literal: Chenggui was also sometimes forgiving in affairs: coin-casting workers often complained that earlier and later supervisors had stolen copper and buried it in the ground, several thousand jin; Chenggui pretended not to accept this, then secretly sent men to dig it up and return it to the office, and did not inquire into their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui could also be forgiving. Coin-casting workers often complained that former and later supervisors had stolen copper and buried thousands of jin in the ground. Chenggui pretended not to accept their account, then secretly sent men to dig it up and return it to the office without punishing anyone.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，朱昂、杜鎬編次館閣書籍，錢若水修祖宗實錄，其後修《冊府元龜》、國史及編著讎校之事，承規悉典領之。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, Zhu Ang and Du Gao arranged the Hall and Library books, Qian Ruoshui edited the Veritable Records of the Ancestors; afterward editing the "Cefu Yuangui," national history, and compiling and collating—Chenggui supervised all of these.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era, Zhu Ang and Du Gao arranged the Hall and Library books and Qian Ruoshui edited the Veritable Records of the Ancestors. Chenggui later supervised all work on the Cefu Yuangui, the national history, and compilation and collation.

sentences.zh: 頗好儒學，喜聚書，間接文士質訪故實，其有名於朝者多見禮待，或密為延薦。

translations.literal: He was quite fond of Confucian learning, delighted in collecting books, and from time to time sought out literati to inquire about historical facts; those with fame at court were often treated with courtesy, or he secretly recommended them for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He was quite fond of Confucian learning and delighted in collecting books. From time to time he sought out literati to inquire about historical facts. Those with fame at court were often treated with courtesy, and he sometimes secretly recommended them for promotion.

sentences.zh: 自寢疾惟以公家之務為念，遺奏求免贈賻詔葬，上甚嗟惜之，遣內臣與鴻臚典喪，親為祭文。

translations.literal: From his sickbed he thought only of public affairs; his final memorial requested exemption from gift grants and edict burial; the emperor deeply lamented him, sent inner attendants with the Minister of Ceremonies to direct the funeral, and personally composed the funerary text.
translations.idiomatic: Even from his sickbed he thought only of public affairs. His final memorial asked to be exempted from gift grants and edict burial. The emperor deeply lamented his death, sent inner attendants with the Minister of Ceremonies to direct the funeral, and personally composed the funerary text.

sentences.zh: 玉清昭應宮成，加贈侍中，遣內侍鄧守恩就墓告祭。

translations.literal: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace was completed, he was additionally posthumously granted Chief Councilor; inner attendant Deng Shou'en was sent to his tomb to announce the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace was completed, he was additionally posthumously granted Chief Councilor, and inner attendant Deng Shou'en was sent to his tomb to announce the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子從願，為西染院使。

translations.literal: His son Congyuan was Director of the Western Dyeing Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congyuan served as Director of the Western Dyeing Bureau.

sentences.zh: 閻承翰，真定人。

translations.literal: Yan Chenghan was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Chenghan was from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中為內侍。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou he was an inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhou Xiande he served as an inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 入宋事太祖，以謹願稱。

translations.literal: Entering Song he served Taizu and was known for diligence and obedience.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Song he served Taizu and was known for diligence and reliability.

sentences.zh: 太宗時擢為殿頭高品，稍遷內侍供奉官、內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Under Taizong he was promoted to Senior Inner Hall Rank, and gradually moved to Inner Attendant Supply Commissioner and Honored Rank of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he was promoted to Senior Inner Hall Rank and gradually rose to Inner Attendant Supply Commissioner and Honored Rank of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 先是，八作司材木頗有隱弊，承翰建議於都城西置事材場，治材以給之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Eight Works Bureau's timber had considerable hidden abuses; Chenghan proposed establishing a timber-processing yard west of the capital to prepare timber for supply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Eight Works Bureau's timber supplies had been riddled with hidden abuses. Chenghan proposed establishing a timber-processing yard west of the capital to prepare timber for official use.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，知廣州徐休復奏轉運使王延範不軌狀，遣承翰馳往同逮捕下獄，就鞫之，考掠過苦，延範遂坐誅。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, Guangzhou prefect Xu Xiufu memorialized about Transport Commissioner Wang Yanfan's disloyal conduct; Chenghan was dispatched post-haste to join in arresting him and sending him to prison; he was interrogated on the spot; the examination and torture were excessively severe, and Yanfan was thus executed.
