translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era, Guangzhou prefect Xu Xiufu memorialized that Transport Commissioner Wang Yanfan had acted disloyally. Chenghan was dispatched post-haste to help arrest him and send him to prison. He was interrogated on the spot under excessively harsh torture, and Yanfan was executed.

sentences.zh: 李順亂蜀，命為川峽招安都監。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled in Shu, he was appointed Overall Supervisor of Pacification for Chuan and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled in Shu, the court appointed him Overall Supervisor of Pacification for Chuan and Xia.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授西京作坊副使。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was granted Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were pacified, he was granted Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.

sentences.zh: 會增募金吾兵，以承翰及劉承蘊分充左右金吾都監兼街仗司事。

translations.literal: When additional Jinwu troops were recruited, Chenghan and Liu Chengyun were appointed respectively as Left and Right Jinwu Overall Supervisors, also handling the Street Halberd Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When additional Jinwu troops were recruited, Chenghan and Liu Chengyun were appointed respectively as Left and Right Jinwu Overall Supervisors, also overseeing the Street Halberd Bureau.

sentences.zh: 俄罷之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward these posts were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long these posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，改西京作坊使、內侍左班副都知。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded, he was made Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and Deputy Director of the Left Class of Inner Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, he was made Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and Deputy Director of the Left Class of Inner Attendants.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，河決鄆州王陵埽，遣承翰護塞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, the Yellow River broke through at Wangling Embankment in Yanzhou; Chenghan was dispatched to supervise the dike repair.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping the Yellow River broke through at Wangling Embankment in Yanzhou, and Chenghan was dispatched to supervise the dike repair.

sentences.zh: 時議徙鄆州以避河患，又詔承翰與工部郎中陳若拙乘傳規度，徙於舊治之東南。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of moving Yanzhou to escape river damage; an edict also ordered Chenghan and Vice Director of the Works Chen Ruozhuo to travel by relay horse to survey and plan, moving it southeast of the old seat.
translations.idiomatic: At the time officials debated moving Yanzhou to escape the river's damage. An edict also ordered Chenghan and Vice Director of the Works Chen Ruozhuo to travel by relay horse to survey the site and plan its relocation southeast of the old seat.

sentences.zh: 五年，入內都知韓守英為鎮、定、高陽關三路排陣都鈐轄，上以其素無執守，議別擇人，因謂宰相曰：「承翰雖無武勇，然涖事勤恪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Inner Director Han Shouying was made Overall Deployment Controller for the three circuits of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass; the emperor held that he had never had steadfast command and discussed choosing another person; he therefore said to the chancellor: "Though Chenghan has no martial valor, yet in handling affairs he is diligent and reverent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Inner Director Han Shouying was made Overall Deployment Controller for the three circuits of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass. The emperor felt that Han had never held steadfast command and discussed choosing someone else. He therefore told the chancellor: "Chenghan may lack martial valor, but in handling affairs he is diligent and reverent.

sentences.zh: 」乃令代守英。

translations.literal: " He then ordered him to replace Shouying.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Chenghan to replace Shouying.

sentences.zh: 時中山屯兵甚眾，艱於飛挽，承翰請鑿渠，計引唐河水自嘉山至定州三十二里，又至蒲陰東六十二里，合沙河經邊吳泊入界河以濟饋運，亦可旁為方田，上嘉而從之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongshan had very many garrison troops and had difficulty with rapid transport; Chenghan requested digging a canal, planning to draw Tang River water from Jiashan to Dingzhou, thirty-two li, then east to Puyin another sixty-two li, joining the Sha River, passing Bianwupo and entering the Border River to aid supply transport; side fields could also be laid out; the emperor praised this and assented.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhongshan had a large garrison and struggled to move supplies quickly. Chenghan proposed digging a canal to draw Tang River water from Jiashan to Dingzhou for thirty-two li, then another sixty-two li east to Puyin, joining the Sha River, passing Bianwupo, and entering the Border River to facilitate supply transport. Side fields could also be laid out along it. The emperor praised the plan and approved it.

sentences.zh: 渠成，人以為便，優詔褒之。

translations.literal: When the canal was completed, people found it convenient; an exceptional edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the canal was completed, people found it convenient, and an exceptional edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 景德初，契丹謀寇順安軍，承翰奉詔發雄、霸精兵，與荊嗣、張延同築壘禦之，俄又遣詣德清軍規度重修城壘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, the Khitan planned to raid Shun'an Army; Chenghan received the edict to mobilize elite troops from Xiong and Ba, and with Jing Si and Zhang Yan jointly built fortifications to defend; soon he was again dispatched to Deqing Army to survey and plan rebuilding the walls and fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingde the Khitan planned to raid Shun'an Army. Chenghan received orders to mobilize elite troops from Xiong and Ba, and with Jing Si and Zhang Yan he built fortifications to defend against them. Soon he was again dispatched to Deqing Army to survey and plan rebuilding the walls and fortifications.

sentences.zh: 車駕北征，承翰先在澶州北城，奏契丹兵在近，請不度河，上不聽，促駕度浮橋。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched north, Chenghan was first at the northern wall of Chenzhou; he memorialized that Khitan troops were near and requested not crossing the river; the emperor did not listen and urged the carriage to cross the pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage marched north, Chenghan was already at the northern wall of Chenzhou. He memorialized that Khitan troops were near and urged that the emperor not cross the river. The emperor would not listen and pressed the carriage to cross the pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 二年，加領廉州刺史，勾當群牧司，多條上馬政，遂兼群牧副使。

translations.literal: In the second year he additionally held Prefect of Lianzhou, managed the Pasturage Bureau, submitted many items on horse policy, and thus also served as Deputy Commissioner of Pasturage.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he additionally held the post of Prefect of Lianzhou and managed the Pasturage Bureau. He submitted many proposals on horse policy and was thus also made Deputy Commissioner of Pasturage.

sentences.zh: 時契丹結好，始置國信司主交聘之事，以承翰領之，多所規置。

translations.literal: At the time when peace was made with the Khitan, the State Credence Bureau was first established to manage diplomatic exchange matters; Chenghan was placed in charge and made many arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was made with the Khitan, the State Credence Bureau was first established to manage diplomatic exchange matters. Chenghan was placed in charge and made many arrangements.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，改西京左藏庫使，充夏州趙德明加恩官告使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, he was changed to Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Storehouse and served as Commissioner bearing the edict of grace for Xiazhou's Zhao Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu reign he was made Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Storehouse and served as Commissioner bearing the edict of grace for Xiazhou's Zhao Deming.

sentences.zh: 還，請於浦洛河置館，以待夏台進奉使，上以荒敻勞役，不許。

translations.literal: On return, he requested establishing a lodge at the Puluo River to receive Xia tribute envoys; the emperor held that the remote waste would burden labor and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he requested establishing a lodge at the Puluo River to receive Xia tribute envoys. The emperor held that the remote wasteland would impose too great a burden on labor and did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷內園使、左班都知，領獎州團練使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Inner Garden Commissioner and Director of the Left Class, holding Regimental Commissioner of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Inner Garden Commissioner and Director of the Left Class, and also held the post of Regimental Commissioner of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 有西京左藏庫副使趙守倫久典廄牧，至是又掌估馬，與承翰聯職任，雖素為姻家，然不相得，遂各訟訴，並付御史臺。

translations.literal: There was Western Capital Left Storehouse Deputy Commissioner Zhao Shoulun, who for long had managed the stables and pasturage; at this time he also managed the horse appraisal office, sharing duties with Chenghan; though they had long been related by marriage, they did not get along, and each sued the other; both cases were sent to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Western Capital Left Storehouse Deputy Commissioner Zhao Shoulun had long managed the stables and pasturage, and at this time he also managed the horse appraisal office, sharing duties with Chenghan. Though they had long been related by marriage, they did not get along and each sued the other. Both cases were sent to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 承翰坐擅用群牧司錢，當贖金三十斤；

translations.literal: Chenghan was convicted of unauthorized use of Pasturage Bureau funds and owed thirty jin redemption fine;
translations.idiomatic: Chenghan was convicted of unauthorized use of Pasturage Bureau funds and was liable for a redemption fine of thirty jin;

sentences.zh: 守倫坐違制移估馬司，當免所居官；

translations.literal: Shoulun was convicted of violating regulations in moving the horse appraisal office and should be stripped of his current office;
translations.idiomatic: Shoulun was convicted of violating regulations in moving the horse appraisal office and was to be stripped of his current office;

sentences.zh: 典吏當杖脊。

translations.literal: The clerks involved should be beaten on the back.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks involved were to be beaten on the back.

sentences.zh: 詔寬其罰：承翰贖金十斤，守倫贖金二十斤，典吏亦降從杖。

translations.literal: An edict mitigated the punishments: Chenghan's redemption fine was ten jin, Shoulun's twenty jin, and the clerks also received reduced corporal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mitigated the punishments: Chenghan's redemption fine was reduced to ten jin, Shoulun's to twenty jin, and the clerks also received reduced corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 群牧都監張繼能、判官陳越田瑴、勾當騏驥院楊保用、估馬楊繼凝皆釋之，製置使陳堯叟特免按問。

translations.literal: Overall Supervisor of Pasturage Zhang Jineng, Judge Chen Yue and Tian Yu, Manager of the Fine Horses Bureau Yang Baoyong, and horse appraiser Yang Jining were all released; Commissioner for Reorganization Chen Yaosou was specially exempted from inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Overall Supervisor of Pasturage Zhang Jineng, Judge Chen Yue and Tian Yu, Manager of the Fine Horses Bureau Yang Baoyong, and horse appraiser Yang Jining were all released. Commissioner for Reorganization Chen Yaosou was specially exempted from inquiry.

sentences.zh: 六年，上製《內侍箴》賜之，承翰表請刻石省中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor composed the "Admonition for Inner Attendants" and granted it to him; Chenghan memorialized requesting it be carved on stone in the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the emperor composed the "Admonition for Inner Attendants" and granted it to him. Chenghan memorialized requesting that it be carved on stone in the provincial office.

sentences.zh: 明年，建應天府為南京，作鴻慶宮，設太祖、太宗像，遣承翰自京奉往。

translations.literal: The next year Yingtian Prefecture was made the Southern Capital, Hongqing Palace was built, and statues of Taizu and Taizong were set up; Chenghan was dispatched from the capital to convey them there.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yingtian Prefecture was made the Southern Capital and Hongqing Palace was built with statues of Taizu and Taizong. Chenghan was dispatched from the capital to convey the statues there.

sentences.zh: 授南作坊使、入內都知。

translations.literal: He was granted Commissioner of Southern Workshops and Inner Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commissioner of Southern Workshops and Inner Director.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈懷州防禦使。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Defense Commissioner of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Defense Commissioner of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 承翰性剛強，所至過於檢察，乏和懿之譽。

translations.literal: Chenghan was by nature stubborn and strong; wherever he went he was excessively investigatory and lacked a reputation for harmony and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghan was by nature stubborn and strong. Wherever he went he was excessively investigatory and never won a reputation for harmony and kindness.

sentences.zh: 子文應，西京左藏庫使。

translations.literal: His son Wenying was Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenying served as Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 秦翰，字仲文，真定獲鹿人。

translations.literal: Qin Han, style name Zhongwen, was a native of Huolu in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Han, style name Zhongwen, was from Huolu in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 十三為黃門，開寶中遷高品。

translations.literal: At thirteen he became a Yellow Gate attendant; in the Kaibao era he was promoted to Senior Rank.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he became a Yellow Gate attendant, and in the Kaibao era he was promoted to Senior Rank.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，崔彥進領眾數萬擊契丹，翰為都監，以善戰聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, Cui Yanjin led tens of thousands to strike the Khitan; Han served as overall supervisor and was known for skill in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, Cui Yanjin led tens of thousands to strike the Khitan. Han served as overall supervisor and became known for skill in battle.

sentences.zh: 太宗因加賞異，謂可屬任。

translations.literal: Taizong therefore added exceptional reward and said he could be entrusted with responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong therefore added exceptional rewards and said that he could be entrusted with important responsibility.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，出為瀛州駐泊，仍管先鋒事，遷入內殿頭高品、鎮、定、高陽關三路排陣都監。

translations.literal: In Yongxi he went out as garrison commander at Yingzhou, still managing vanguard affairs; he was promoted to Senior Inner Hall Head Rank and Overall Supervisor of Battle Formations for the three circuits of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi he was sent out as garrison commander at Yingzhou while still managing vanguard affairs. He was promoted to Senior Inner Hall Head Rank and Overall Supervisor of Battle Formations for the three circuits of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，補入內押班。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was appointed to the Inner Escort Class.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was added to the Inner Escort Class.

sentences.zh: 趙保忠叛，命李繼隆率師問罪，翰監護其軍。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baozhong rebelled, Li Jilong was ordered to lead an army to punish him; Han supervised and escorted his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baozhong rebelled, Li Jilong was ordered to lead an army to punish him, and Han supervised and escorted the army.

sentences.zh: 次延州，翰慮保忠遁逸，即乘驛先往，矯詔安撫以緩其陰計。

translations.literal: When they halted at Yanzhou, Han feared Baozhong would escape; he immediately rode relay post ahead, falsely issuing an edict of pacification to slow his secret plans.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Yanzhou, Han feared Baozhong would escape. He immediately rode relay post ahead and falsely issued an edict of pacification to slow Baozhong's secret plans.

sentences.zh: 王師至，翰又諷保忠以地主之禮郊迎，因並驅而出，保忠遂就擒，以功加崇儀副使。

translations.literal: When the imperial army arrived, Han also hinted to Baozhong to welcome them in the countryside with the rites due a local lord; thus they drove out together, and Baozhong was then captured; for merit he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of Honored Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army arrived, Han also hinted to Baozhong to welcome them in the countryside with the rites due a local lord. They then rode out together, and Baozhong was captured. For this merit Han was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of Honored Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 至道初，為靈、環、慶州、清遠軍四路都監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao he was Overall Supervisor of the four routes of Ling, Huan, Qingzhou, and Qingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhidao reign he was Overall Supervisor of the four routes of Ling, Huan, Qingzhou, and Qingyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加洛苑使、入內副都知。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded he was additionally made Luoyuan Commissioner and Deputy Inner Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne he was additionally made Luoyuan Commissioner and Deputy Inner Director.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，河朔用兵，以為鎮、定、高陽關排陣都監，敗契丹於莫州東，追斬數萬，盡奪所掠老幼。

translations.literal: In Xianping, when the Hebei region saw military action, he was made Battle Formation Supervisor for Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass; he defeated the Khitan east of Mozhou, pursued and killed tens of thousands, and fully recovered the old and young they had plundered.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping, when the Hebei region saw military action, he was made Battle Formation Supervisor for Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass. He defeated the Khitan east of Mozhou, pursued and killed tens of thousands, and fully recovered the old and young they had plundered.

sentences.zh: 詔褒之，徙定州行營鈐轄。

translations.literal: An edict praised him; he was transferred to Campaign Deployment Controller at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him, and he was transferred to Campaign Deployment Controller at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王均之亂，為川峽招安巡檢使。

translations.literal: In Wang Jun's rebellion he was Pacification and Inspection Commissioner for Chuan and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Jun's rebellion he served as Pacification and Inspection Commissioner for Chuan and Xia.

sentences.zh: 時上官正與石普不協，翰恐生事，為曉譬和解之。

translations.literal: At the time Shangguan Zheng and Shi Pu were at odds; Han feared trouble would arise and personally reasoned with them to reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shangguan Zheng and Shi Pu were at odds. Han feared trouble would arise and personally reasoned with them until they reconciled.

sentences.zh: 親督眾擊賊，中流矢不卻，五戰五捷，遂克益州，上手劄勞問。

translations.literal: He personally led the troops to strike the rebels, was struck by a flowing arrow but did not retreat, won five battles in five engagements, and thus captured Yizhou; the emperor sent a personal letter of consolation and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led the troops against the rebels, was struck by an arrow but did not retreat, won five battles in five engagements, and captured Yizhou. The emperor sent him a personal letter of praise and inquiry.

sentences.zh: 翼日，進至廣都，斬首千餘級，獲馬數千匹。

translations.literal: The next day he advanced to Guangdu, beheaded over a thousand, and captured several thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he advanced to Guangdu, beheaded more than a thousand enemies, and captured several thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，遷內園使，領恩州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was promoted to Inner Garden Commissioner and held Prefect of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was promoted to Inner Garden Commissioner and also held the post of Prefect of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮、定、高陽關前陣鈐轄，又徙後陣。

translations.literal: He went out as Forward Deployment Controller for Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, then was transferred to the rear formation.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Forward Deployment Controller for Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, then was transferred to the rear formation.

sentences.zh: 破契丹二萬眾於威虜軍西，俘其鐵林大將等十五人。

translations.literal: He defeated twenty thousand Khitan west of Weilu Army and captured fifteen men including their Iron Forest general.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated twenty thousand Khitan west of Weilu Army and captured fifteen men, including their Iron Forest general.

sentences.zh: 又為邠寧、涇原路鈐轄兼安撫都監，率所部按行山外，召戎落酋帥，諭以恩信，凡三千餘帳相率內附。

translations.literal: He also served as Deployment Controller of Binning and Jingyuan Circuits and Overall Supervisor of Pacification; he led his troops to patrol beyond the mountains, summoned tribal chieftains, instructed them with grace and trust, and altogether more than three thousand tents came over in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Deployment Controller of Binning and Jingyuan Circuits and Overall Supervisor of Pacification. He led his troops to patrol beyond the mountains, summoned tribal chieftains, and instructed them with grace and trust. More than three thousand tents came over in succession.

sentences.zh: 未幾，康奴族拒命，翰與陳興、許均深入擊之，斬級數千，焚其廬帳，獲牛馬甚眾。

translations.literal: Before long the Kangnu tribe defied orders; Han with Chen Xing and Xu Jun penetrated deep to strike them, beheaded several thousand, burned their tents, and captured very many cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Kangnu tribe defied orders. Han with Chen Xing and Xu Jun penetrated deep to strike them, beheaded several thousand, burned their tents, and captured a great many cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 復與陳興、曹瑋襲殺童埋軍主於武延咸泊川。

translations.literal: Again with Chen Xing and Cao Wei he launched a surprise attack and killed the military commander Tongmai at Wuyan Xianbo River.
translations.idiomatic: Again with Chen Xing and Cao Wei he launched a surprise attack and killed the military commander Tongmai on the Wuyan Xianbo River.

sentences.zh: 詔書加獎，賜錦袍、金帶、白金五百兩、帛五百匹。

translations.literal: An edict letter added commendation; he was granted a brocade robe, gold belt, five hundred taels of white gold, and five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict letter added further commendation. He was granted a brocade robe, a gold belt, five hundred taels of white gold, and five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 景德初，車駕將北巡，先遣翰乘傳往澶、魏裁制兵要，許便宜從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, when the imperial carriage would make a northern tour, Han was first dispatched by relay horse to Chen and Wei to decide military essentials, permitted to act as expedient required.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingde, when the imperial carriage was about to make a northern tour, Han was first dispatched by relay horse to Chen and Wei to decide military essentials, with permission to act as expedient required.

sentences.zh: 俄充邢洺路鈐轄，與大軍會德清軍，張掎角之勢。

translations.literal: Shortly he served as Deployment Controller of Xing and Ming Circuits, joined the great army at Deqing Army, and spread pincer formation.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he served as Deployment Controller of Xing and Ming Circuits, joined the main army at Deqing Army, and deployed in pincer formation.

sentences.zh: 又召為駕前西面排陣鈐轄，管勾大陣。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Forward Western Battle Formation Deployment Controller before the imperial carriage, managing the great formation.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned as Forward Western Battle Formation Deployment Controller before the imperial carriage to manage the great formation.

sentences.zh: 翰即督眾環城浚溝洫以拒契丹。

translations.literal: Han immediately directed the troops to dig moats around the city to resist the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Han immediately directed the troops to dig moats around the city to hold off the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 功畢，契丹兵果暴至，翰不脫甲胄七十餘日，契丹乞和，凱旋，留泊澶州。

translations.literal: When the work was complete, Khitan troops indeed suddenly arrived; Han did not remove his armor for more than seventy days; the Khitan sued for peace; victorious return; remained stationed at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was complete, Khitan troops indeed suddenly arrived. Han did not remove his armor for more than seventy days. The Khitan sued for peace, the army returned in victory, and he remained stationed at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 月餘，令率所部兵還京師，加宮苑使、入內都知。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was ordered to lead his troops back to the capital; he was promoted to Palace Garden Commissioner and Inner Director.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he was ordered to lead his troops back to the capital and was promoted to Palace Garden Commissioner and Inner Director.

sentences.zh: 出為涇、原、儀、渭鈐轄。

translations.literal: He went out as Deployment Controller of Jing, Yuan, Yi, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Deployment Controller of Jing, Yuan, Yi, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 先是，西鄙無藩籬之蔽，翰規度要害，鑿巨塹，計工三十萬，役卒數年而成，不煩於民。

translations.literal: Earlier the western frontier had no barrier protection; Han surveyed key points, dug a great trench—estimated thirty thousand man-days—and corvée soldiers completed it in several years without troubling the people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the western frontier had no barrier protection. Han surveyed key points and dug a great trench, estimated at thirty thousand man-days. Corvée soldiers completed it over several years without troubling the people.

sentences.zh: 就遷皇城使、入內都知。

translations.literal: On the spot he was transferred to Director of the Imperial City and Inner Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately transferred to Director of the Imperial City and Inner Director.

sentences.zh: 以翰在邊久，宣力勤盡，特置是名以寵異焉。

translations.literal: Because Han had long been on the frontier exerting himself diligently and exhaustively, this title was specially created to honor him exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: Because Han had long served on the frontier with tireless diligence, this title was specially created to honor him exceptionally.

sentences.zh: 翰表讓，不聽。

translations.literal: Han memorialized to decline; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Han memorialized to decline the honor, but the request was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，求從東封，手詔諭以西垂委任之異。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he requested to follow the eastern Fengshan; a personal edict explained the special trust placed in him for the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu reign he requested to follow the eastern Fengshan ceremony. A personal edict explained the special trust placed in him for the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 改昭宣使，又為群牧副使，祀汾陰。

translations.literal: He was changed to Zhaoxuan Commissioner, again served as Deputy Commissioner of Pasturage, and attended the sacrifice at Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Zhaoxuan Commissioner, again served as Deputy Commissioner of Pasturage, and attended the sacrifice at Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 是歲，夏州屬戶有擾境上者，即日遣翰往脽上按視，遍巡邊部。

translations.literal: That year Xiazhou dependent households disturbed the border; that same day Han was dispatched to the frontier to inspect, touring the border regions comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xiazhou dependent households disturbed the border. That same day Han was dispatched to the frontier to inspect and comprehensively tour the border regions.

sentences.zh: 及翰至，事寧，復還扈從，凡行在諸司細務，悉令裁決，不須中覆。

translations.literal: When Han arrived matters were settled; he returned again to attend the imperial procession; all minor business of the various offices at the traveling court was ordered decided by him without needing central review.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arrived the matter was settled. He returned again to attend the imperial procession, and all minor business of the various offices at the traveling court was ordered decided by him without needing central review.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，加領平州團練使，奉祀毫州，掌如汾陰。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, he was additionally appointed Military Training Commissioner of Pingzhou, charged to conduct sacrifice at Bozhou, with duties like those at Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, he was further made Military Training Commissioner of Pingzhou and charged with conducting the sacrifice at Bozhou, with responsibilities like those he had held at Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 八年，營葺大內，詔翰參領其事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the inner palace was being repaired and built, an edict ordered Han to participate in leading the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, as the inner palace was being repaired and rebuilt, the emperor ordered Han to help oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 閏六月，暴卒於內庭之廨，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month he died suddenly at the office in the inner court, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month he died suddenly in his office within the inner court, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 上甚悼惜，為之泣下。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned and regretted it, weeping for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply and wept.

sentences.zh: 贈貝州觀察使，賻襚加等。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Observation Commissioner of Beizhou; condolence goods and burial accoutrements were increased by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Observation Commissioner of Beizhou, and the gifts of condolence and burial raiment were raised by one rank.

sentences.zh: 修內畢，詔遣使以襲衣、金帶賜其家。

translations.literal: When the inner-palace repairs were completed, an edict dispatched envoys to bestow upon his family burial robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner-palace repairs were finished, the emperor sent envoys to bestow burial robes and a gold belt upon his family.

sentences.zh: 翰倜儻有武力，以方略自任。

translations.literal: Han was dashing and possessed martial prowess, taking strategy and planning upon himself as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Han was bold and capable in arms, and held himself responsible for strategy and planning.

sentences.zh: 前後戰鬥，身被四十九創。

translations.literal: In battles before and after, his body received forty-nine wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Over many battles his body bore forty-nine wounds.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷之未賓也，翰因使常出入其帳中，無疑間，嘗白太宗言：「臣一內官不足惜，願手刺此賊，死無所恨。

translations.literal: Before Li Jiqian had submitted, because of his missions Han often entered and exited his tent without arousing suspicion, and once reported to Emperor Taizong, saying: "Your subject, a single inner-palace official, is not worth regretting; I wish to stab this brigand with my own hand, and would die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Before Li Jiqian had submitted to the court, Han, on his missions, often went in and out of Jiqian's tent without arousing suspicion. Once he reported to Emperor Taizong: "I am only one inner-palace official and not worth sparing; I wish to stab this rebel with my own hand, and would die without regret.

sentences.zh: 」太宗深嘉其忠。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor greatly praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 翰性溫良謙謹，接人以誠信，群帥有剛狠不和者，翰皆得其歡心。

translations.literal: Han was by nature gentle, kind, modest, and careful; he received people with sincerity and trust; among the commanders there were tough and fierce ones who did not get along, yet Han won the affection of all.
translations.idiomatic: Han was gentle, modest, and careful by nature, and treated others with sincerity and trust. Even among commanders who were harsh and difficult to get along with, he won their goodwill.

sentences.zh: 輕財好施，與將士同休戚，能得眾心，皆樂為用。

translations.literal: He thought lightly of wealth and loved to give; he shared joys and sorrows with officers and soldiers, could win men's hearts, and all gladly served under him.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for money and loved to give it away. He shared hardship and comfort with his officers and soldiers, won their hearts, and all were glad to serve him.

sentences.zh: 其歿也，禁旅有泣下者。

translations.literal: When he died, there were those among the palace guard who wept.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, some among the palace guard wept.

sentences.zh: 九年，重贈彰國軍節度，詔楊億撰碑文，億以其不蓄財，表辭所贄物，雖朝廷不許，而時論美之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was posthumously granted again Jiedushi of the Zhangguo Army; an edict ordered Yang Yi to compose the epitaph; Yi, because Han had not accumulated wealth, memorialized declining the customary gift objects; though the court did not permit it, public opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was posthumously made Jiedushi of the Zhangguo Army, and the emperor ordered Yang Yi to write his epitaph. Yi, noting that Han had never hoarded wealth, submitted a memorial declining the customary payment for the inscription. The court refused, but contemporaries praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 子懷誌，內殿崇班。

translations.literal: His son Huaizhi held the post of Inner Hall Honored Companion.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaizhi served as Inner Hall Honored Companion.

sentences.zh: 周懷政，并州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Huaizheng, a native of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huaizheng was a native of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父紹忠，以黃門事太宗，從征河東，得懷政於亂屍間，養為子。

translations.literal: His father Shaozhong, serving as a Yellow Gate attendant to Taizong, on the campaign to Hedong found Huaizheng among the corpses in the chaos and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaozhong served Taizong as a Yellow Gate attendant. On the campaign in Hedong he found Huaizheng among the dead in the chaos and raised him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 給事禁中，累至入內高品。

translations.literal: He served in the inner palace and rose through posts to Inner-palace Senior Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the inner palace and rose step by step to Inner-palace Senior Attendant.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，真宗東封，命修行宮頓遞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, when Emperor Zhenzong performed the eastern Fengshan, he was ordered to manage traveling palaces and relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu reign, when Emperor Zhenzong performed the eastern Fengshan rites, Huaizheng was ordered to oversee the traveling palaces and relay stations along the route.

sentences.zh: 及奉泰山天書馳驛赴闕，轉殿頭。

translations.literal: When bearing the Heavenly Writ from Mount Tai, he rushed by post to the capital and was promoted to Hall Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When he carried the Heavenly Writ from Mount Tai back to court by post relay, he was promoted to Hall Chief.

sentences.zh: 天書每出宮，與皇甫繼明並為夾侍。

translations.literal: Whenever the Heavenly Writ left the palace, he and Huangfu Jiming served jointly as flank attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Heavenly Writ was taken out of the palace, he and Huangfu Jiming served together as flank attendants.

sentences.zh: 東封禮成，與內殿崇班康宗元留泰山，修圜台，轉入內西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: When the eastern Fengshan rites were completed, he and Inner Hall Honored Companion Kang Zongyuan remained at Mount Tai to repair the Round Altar, and he was promoted to Inner Western Head Attendant-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern Fengshan rites were finished, he and Inner Hall Honored Companion Kang Zongyuan stayed behind at Mount Tai to repair the Round Altar, and he was promoted to Inner Western Head Attendant-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，轉東頭。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice at Fenyin, he was transferred to Eastern Head.
translations.idiomatic: At the Fenyin sacrifice he was transferred to Eastern Head attendant.

sentences.zh: 六年，劉承規卒，擢內殿崇班、入內押班、勾當皇城司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Liu Chenggui died, he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Companion, Inner-palace Escort Chief, and Acting Director of the Imperial City Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, after Liu Chenggui died, he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Companion, Inner-palace Escort Chief, and Acting Director of the Imperial City Office.

sentences.zh: 會朝謁太清宮，與閻承翰等同管勾大內事。

translations.literal: When the court visited the Taichong Palace, he together with Yan Chenghan and others jointly managed inner-palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the court paid homage at the Taichong Palace, he and Yan Chenghan and others jointly managed inner-palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年，奉天書摹刻於乾元殿，為刻玉都監，又為修兗州景靈宮、太極觀都監，俄遷內殿承製。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Heavenly Writ was copied and carved in the Qianyuan Hall, he served as Director General of Jade Carving; he was also Director General for repairing the Jingling Palace and Taiji Abbey in Yanzhou; soon he was promoted to Inner Hall Manufacture Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Heavenly Writ was copied and carved in the Qianyuan Hall, he served as Director General of Jade Carving. He was also made Director General for repairing the Jingling Palace and Taiji Abbey in Yanzhou, and soon afterward was promoted to Inner Hall Manufacture Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是冬，命起居舍人、知制誥盛度為會真宮醮告使，懷政為都監。

translations.literal: That winter, the Court Diarist and Drafter of Edicts Sheng Du was appointed Envoy for Prayer at Huizhen Palace, with Huaizheng as Director General.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Court Diarist and Drafter of Edicts Sheng Du was appointed prayer envoy for Huizhen Palace, with Huaizheng as director general.

sentences.zh: 還，為玉清昭應宮都監兼掌景靈宮、會靈觀使。

translations.literal: On return he served as Director General of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace and concurrently managed the Jingling Palace and Huiling Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became Director General of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace and concurrently oversaw the Jingling Palace and Huiling Abbey.

sentences.zh: 刻玉成，遷如京副使。

translations.literal: When the jade carving was completed, he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner on Capital Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the jade carving was finished, he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner on Capital Affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，建資善堂，以懷政為都監。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Zishan Hall was built, Huaizheng was made Director General.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Zishan Hall was built, Huaizheng was appointed its director general.

sentences.zh: 壽丘宮觀成，優賜襲衣、金帶，遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: When the Shouqiu palace and abbey were completed, he was graciously bestowed burial robes and a gold belt and promoted to Honored Ceremonial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shouqiu palace and abbey were completed, he was graciously granted burial robes and a gold belt and promoted to Honored Ceremonial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天禧大禮，又為修奉寶冊都監，加領長州刺史，是冬，遷洛苑使。

translations.literal: For the Tianxi grand ceremony he again served as Director General for preparing the precious register, and was additionally appointed prefect of Changzhou; that winter he was promoted to Luoyuan Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For the Tianxi grand ceremony he again served as director general for preparing the precious register and was additionally made prefect of Changzhou. That winter he was promoted to Luoyuan Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年春，遷左藏庫使。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, he was promoted to Commissioner of the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he was promoted to Commissioner of the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇太子，命為入內副都知、管勾左右春坊，轉左騏驥使。

translations.literal: When Renzong was crown prince, he was appointed Deputy Chief of Inner Attendants and Acting Director of the Left and Right Eastern Palaces, and was promoted to Left Qiji Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, Huaizheng was appointed Deputy Chief of Inner Attendants and Acting Director of the Left and Right Eastern Palaces, and was promoted to Left Qiji Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，領英州團練使，加昭宣使。

translations.literal: In the third year he held the post of Military Training Commissioner of Yingzhou and was made Zhaoxuan Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Military Training Commissioner of Yingzhou and promoted to Zhaoxuan Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 懷政日侍內廷，權任尤盛，於是附會者頗眾，往往言事獲從，同列位望居右者，必排抑之。

translations.literal: Huaizheng daily attended the inner court and his power and responsibility were especially great; accordingly those who attached themselves to him were quite numerous; his proposals were often followed, and colleagues of higher standing or reputation he inevitably suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizheng attended the inner court every day, and his power grew especially great. Many attached themselves to him, and his proposals were often accepted. Colleagues of higher rank or reputation he always pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 中外帑庫皆得專取，因多入其家。

translations.literal: He could take exclusively from treasuries at court and in the provinces, so much entered his household.
translations.idiomatic: He was able to draw freely from treasuries at court and in the provinces, and much of it found its way into his home.

sentences.zh: 性識凡近，酷信妖妄。

translations.literal: His nature and judgment were ordinary and shallow; he deeply believed in demonic falsehoods.
translations.idiomatic: His mind was shallow, and he was fanatically credulous of occult fraud.

sentences.zh: 有朱能者，本單州團練使田敏廝養，為人凶狡，遂賂懷政親信，得見，因與侍卒姚斌妄談神懌以訹之。

translations.literal: There was a Zhu Neng, originally a menial of Tian Min, Military Training Commissioner of Danzhou; he was fierce and cunning by nature; he bribed Huaizheng's trusted intimates to gain an audience, then together with the attendant soldier Yao Bin talked wildly of divine tranquility to intimidate him.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Zhu Neng, originally a servant of Tian Min, Military Training Commissioner of Danzhou. He was violent and cunning. He bribed Huaizheng's trusted followers to gain an audience, then together with the attendant soldier Yao Bin spun tales of divine portents to frighten and deceive him.

sentences.zh: 懷政大惑，援能至禦藥使、領階州刺史。

translations.literal: Huaizheng was greatly deluded, and promoted Neng to Imperial Pharmacy Commissioner and additionally made him prefect of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizheng was thoroughly taken in and promoted Neng to Imperial Pharmacy Commissioner, additionally making him prefect of Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 俄於終南山修道觀，與劉益輩造符命，托神言國家休咎，否臧大臣。

translations.literal: Soon at Zhongnan Mountain he built a Daoist abbey, and with Liu Yi and others fabricated prophecy tokens, passing off divine words on the state's fortune and misfortune, approving or condemning great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he built a Daoist abbey on Zhongnan Mountain. With Liu Yi and others he forged prophetic tokens, claiming divine pronouncements on the fortunes of the state and passing judgment on high ministers.

sentences.zh: 時寇準鎮永興，能為巡檢，倚準舊望，欲實其事。

translations.literal: At the time Kou Zhun commanded at Yongxing; Neng served as inspector, relying on Kou's former prestige, hoping to make the affair real.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Kou Zhun was stationed at Yongxing, and Neng served as an inspector. Relying on Kou's former standing, he hoped to give the scheme substance.

sentences.zh: 準好勝，喜其附己，多依違之。

translations.literal: Kou loved to compete and was pleased that Neng attached to him, and often wavered accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Kou was competitive by nature and was pleased that Neng sided with him, so he often went along without firm judgment.

sentences.zh: 朝臣屢言懷政之妄，真宗含忍不斥，然漸疏遠之。

translations.literal: Court ministers repeatedly spoke of Huaizheng's extravagance; Zhenzong tolerated and did not rebuke him, yet gradually grew distant.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers repeatedly reported Huaizheng's misconduct, but Zhenzong endured it without rebuke and only gradually kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 懷政憂懼，時使小黃門自禁中出，詐稱宣召，入內東門，坐別室，久之而還，以欺同類。

translations.literal: Huaizheng was anxious and afraid; sometimes he would send a junior yellow-gate attendant out from the inner palace, falsely claiming an imperial summons, entering the inner eastern gate, sitting in a separate room, and after a long time returning, to deceive his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Anxious and afraid, Huaizheng sometimes sent a junior yellow-gate attendant out of the inner palace with a false claim of imperial summons. The attendant would enter the inner eastern gate, sit in a side room for a long while, then return—purely to deceive his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 會準為相，逾年而罷，懷政愈畏獲譴，不自安。

translations.literal: When Kou became chief minister, after more than a year he was dismissed; Huaizheng grew ever more afraid of punishment and was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Kou became chief minister he was dismissed after little more than a year. Huaizheng grew ever more afraid of being punished and could not rest easy.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，與弟禮賓副使懷信謀潛召客省使楊崇勳、內殿承製楊懷吉、閣門祗候楊懷玉會皇城司，期以二十五日竊發，殺丁謂等，復相寇準，奉真宗為太上皇，傳位太子。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, he and his younger brother Deputy Protocol Commissioner Huaixin plotted secretly to summon Guest Reception Commissioner Yang Chongxun, Inner Hall Manufacture Commissioner Yang Huaiji, and Gatekeeper Attendant Yang Huaiyu to meet at the Imperial City Office, planning on the twenty-fifth to launch a covert rebellion, kill Ding Wei and others, restore Kou Zhun as chief minister, install Zhenzong as retired emperor, and transfer the throne to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year he and his younger brother, Deputy Protocol Commissioner Huaixin, secretly summoned Guest Reception Commissioner Yang Chongxun, Inner Hall Manufacture Commissioner Yang Huaiji, and Gatekeeper Attendant Yang Huaiyu to meet at the Imperial City Office. They planned to rise on the twenty-fifth, kill Ding Wei and others, restore Kou Zhun as chief minister, install Zhenzong as retired emperor, and pass the throne to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 前夕，崇勳、懷吉詣丁謂第密告之，謂即夜偕崇勳、懷吉至曹利用第計議，翌日，利用入奏，真宗怒，命收懷政。

translations.literal: The night before, Chongxun and Huaiji went to Ding Wei's residence and secretly reported it; Ding that same night went with Chongxun and Huaiji to Cao Liyong's residence to discuss plans; the next day Liyong entered to memorialize; Zhenzong was angered and ordered Huaizheng arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The night before, Chongxun and Huaiji went to Ding Wei's house and secretly informed him. Ding went that same night with Chongxun and Huaiji to Cao Liyong's residence to plan their response. The next day Liyong entered the palace to report it. Zhenzong was enraged and ordered Huaizheng arrested.

sentences.zh: 令宣徽北院使曹瑋與崇勳於禦藥院鞫訊，具伏。

translations.literal: He ordered Xuanhui Northern Court Commissioner Cao Wei and Chongxun to interrogate him at the Imperial Pharmacy Courtyard; he fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xuanhui Northern Court Commissioner Cao Wei and Chongxun to interrogate him at the Imperial Pharmacy Courtyard, and Huaizheng confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 帝坐承明殿臨問，懷政但祈哀而已，命斬於城西普安寺。

translations.literal: The emperor sat at Chenming Hall and questioned him in person; Huaizheng only pleaded for mercy; he was ordered executed at Pu'an Temple west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him in person at Chenming Hall. Huaizheng could only beg for mercy. He was ordered executed at Pu'an Temple west of the city.

sentences.zh: 父內殿承製紹忠及懷信並杖配復岳州，子侄勒停，貲產沒官。

translations.literal: His father Inner Hall Manufacture Commissioner Shaozhong and Huaixin were both beaten with the staff and exiled to Yuezhou; sons and nephews were ordered to cease office; property was confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Inner Hall Manufacture Commissioner Shaozhong, and Huaixin were both flogged and exiled to Yuezhou. Sons and nephews were barred from office, and their property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 朱能父左武衛將軍致仕諤、母周氏，罰銅百斤，子守昱、守吉分配邵、蔡、道州。

translations.literal: Zhu Neng's father, retired Left Martial Guard General E, and mother Lady Zhou were fined one hundred jin of copper; sons Shouyu and Shouji were assigned respectively to Shao, Cai, and Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Neng's father, the retired Left Martial Guard General E, and his mother Lady Zhou were fined one hundred jin of copper. His sons Shouyu and Shouji were exiled to Shao, Cai, and Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 懷政仆使、親從並杖配海島、遠州，部下使臣貶秩有差。

translations.literal: Huaizheng's domestic servants and personal followers were all beaten and exiled to island and distant prefectures; subordinate envoys were demoted in rank to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizheng's servants and personal followers were all flogged and exiled to island outposts and distant prefectures. Subordinate envoys were demoted in rank to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 懷政之未敗也，紹忠嘗詬之曰：「斫頭豎子終累我！

translations.literal: Before Huaizheng's downfall, Shaozhong once reviled him, saying: "Head-chopping brat, you'll ruin me in the end!
translations.idiomatic: Before Huaizheng's fall, Shaozhong once cursed him: "You reckless fool—you'll ruin me yet!

sentences.zh: 」懷信謂之曰：「兄前事必敗，宜早詣上首實，庶獲輕典。

translations.literal: " Huaixin said to him: "Brother, your prior affair is bound to fail; you ought soon to go before the emperor and confess the truth, that you may perhaps receive lighter punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Huaixin told him: "Brother, your earlier schemes are bound to fail. You should go to the emperor at once and confess everything—you may yet receive a lighter sentence.

sentences.zh: 」及其謀亂，又泣拜止之，不聽，故皆得免死。

translations.literal: " When the plot for rebellion arose, he again wept and bowed to stop him; Huaizheng would not listen; therefore they all escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: " When the rebellion was plotted, he wept and bowed again to stop him, but Huaizheng would not listen. For this reason they all escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 右街僧錄澄遠以預聞妖詐，決杖黥配郴州。

translations.literal: Senior Monk Registrar of the Right Street Chengyuan, for having foreknowledge of the demonic fraud, was sentenced to beating, tattooing, and exile to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Monk Registrar of the Right Street Chengyuan, for having known of the occult fraud in advance, was flogged, tattooed, and exiled to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 內供奉官譚元吉、高品王德信、高班胡允則、黃門楊允文與懷政協同妖妄，皆杖配遠州。

translations.literal: Inner Attendant-in-Waiting Tan Yuanji, Senior Attendant Wang Dexin, Senior Escort Hu Yunze, and Yellow Gate Yang Yunwen, who together with Huaizheng indulged in demonic falsehoods, were all beaten and exiled to distant prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Attendant-in-Waiting Tan Yuanji, Senior Attendant Wang Dexin, Senior Escort Hu Yunze, and Yellow Gate Yang Yunwen, who together with Huaizheng indulged in occult fraud, were all flogged and exiled to distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 入內押班鄭誌誠與能書問往還，削兩任，配房州。

translations.literal: Inner Escort Chief Zheng Zhicheng exchanged letters with Neng; two ranks were stripped; he was exiled to Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Escort Chief Zheng Zhicheng had exchanged letters with Neng. Two ranks were stripped from him and he was exiled to Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入內供奉官石承慶嘗為懷政所召，夜二鼓不下皇城門鑰以待，黃門黃守忠見之，戒門卒勿納，至是言其事，承慶坐削兩任，配宿州。

translations.literal: Inner Attendant-in-Waiting Shi Chengqing had once been summoned by Huaizheng; at the second watch of the night the Imperial City gate lock was not lowered to await him; Yellow Gate Huang Shouzhong saw this and warned the gate soldiers not to admit him; at this time he reported the matter; Chengqing was punished by stripping two ranks and exiled to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Attendant-in-Waiting Shi Chengqing had once been summoned by Huaizheng. At the second watch of the night the Imperial City gate was kept unlocked waiting for him. Yellow Gate Huang Shouzhong saw this and ordered the gate guards not to let him in. Now he reported the matter, and Chengqing was stripped of two ranks and exiled to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊懷玉次日始詣樞密院自陳，責授侍禁、杭州都監。

translations.literal: Yang Huaiyu only the next day went to the Bureau of Military Affairs to confess himself; he was demoted to Palace Guard and Hangzhou Director.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huaiyu did not go to the Bureau of Military Affairs to confess until the next day. He was demoted to Palace Guard and made Hangzhou Director.

sentences.zh: 擢崇勳內客省使、桂州觀察使，懷吉如京使，賜以金帶、金銀。

translations.literal: Chongxun was promoted to Inner Guest Reception Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Guizhou; Huaiji was made Capital Affairs Commissioner; they were bestowed gold belts and gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun was promoted to Inner Guest Reception Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Guizhou. Huaiji was made Capital Affairs Commissioner. Both were granted gold belts and gifts of gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 懷政既誅，亟遣入內供奉官盧守明、鄧文慶馳驛永興，捕朱能。

translations.literal: Once Huaizheng had been executed, envoys were urgently dispatched—Inner Attendants-in-Waiting Lu Shouming and Deng Wenqing galloping by post to Yongxing to capture Zhu Neng.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Huaizheng had been executed, the court urgently dispatched Inner Attendants-in-Waiting Lu Shouming and Deng Wenqing by post relay to Yongxing to capture Zhu Neng.

sentences.zh: 劉益、李貴、康玉、唐信，道士王先、張用和悉免死，配遠州。

translations.literal: Liu Yi, Li Gui, Kang Yu, Tang Xin, and Daoist priests Wang Xian and Zhang Yonghe all escaped death and were exiled to distant prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, Li Gui, Kang Yu, Tang Xin, and the Daoist priests Wang Xian and Zhang Yonghe were all spared execution and exiled to distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 能偵知使者至，衷甲出，殺守明以叛。

translations.literal: Neng learned that envoys had arrived, put on armor beneath his robes and went out, killed Shouming and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Neng learned that the envoys had arrived. He donned hidden armor, went out, killed Shouming, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 詔遣內殿承製江德明、入內供奉官於德潤發兵捕之，能入桑林自縊死。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Inner Hall Manufacture Commissioner Jiang Deming and Inner Attendant-in-Waiting Yu Derun to raise troops and capture him; Neng entered a mulberry grove and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Inner Hall Manufacture Commissioner Jiang Deming and Inner Attendant-in-Waiting Yu Derun to raise troops and capture him. Neng fled into a mulberry grove and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 永興、乾耀都巡檢供奉官李興、本軍十將張順斷能及其子首以獻，補興閣門祗候，順牢城都頭。

translations.literal: Yongxing and Qianyao Chief Inspectors Attendant-in-Waiting Li Xing and the army's Ten-general Zhang Shun cut off the heads of Neng and his son and presented them; Xing was appointed Gatekeeper Attendant, Shun Fortress Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing and Qianyao Chief Inspectors Attendant-in-Waiting Li Xing and the army Ten-general Zhang Shun cut off the heads of Neng and his son and presented them. Xing was appointed Gatekeeper Attendant and Shun Fortress Commander.

sentences.zh: 以劉益等十一人黨能害中使，磔於市。

translations.literal: Liu Yi and eleven others who sided with Neng in harming the imperial envoy were dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi and eleven others who aided Neng in killing the imperial envoy were dismembered in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 王先、李貴、唐信、張用和八人皆處斬。

translations.literal: Wang Xian, Li Gui, Tang Xin, Zhang Yonghe, and eight persons in all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian, Li Gui, Tang Xin, Zhang Yonghe, and eight others in all were executed.

sentences.zh: 能母妻子弟皆決杖配隸，閣門祗候穆介、知永興軍府朱巽、轉運使梅詢劉楚、知鳳翔府臧奎等坐與懷政、能交結相稱薦，皆論罪。

translations.literal: Neng's mother, wife, children, and younger brothers were all beaten, exiled, and reduced to bondage; Gatekeeper Attendant Mu Jie, Yongxing military prefect Zhu Xun, transport commissioners Mei Xun and Liu Chu, and Fengxiang prefect Zang Kui and others, for associating with Huaizheng and Neng and mutually recommending each other, were all punished according to crime.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's mother, wife, children, and younger brothers were all flogged, exiled, and reduced to servitude. Gatekeeper Attendant Mu Jie, Yongxing military prefect Zhu Xun, transport commissioners Mei Xun and Liu Chu, Fengxiang prefect Zang Kui, and others who had associated with Huaizheng and Neng and exchanged mutual recommendations were all punished according to their offenses.

sentences.zh: 降寇準太常卿，再貶道州。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun was demoted to Minister of Ceremonies, then again demoted to Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun was demoted to Minister of Ceremonies and then demoted again to Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 凡朝士及永興、鳳翔官吏與準厚善者，悉降黜焉。

translations.literal: All court officials and Yongxing and Fengxiang officers who were close and friendly with Kou were altogether demoted and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: All court officials and officers of Yongxing and Fengxiang who had been close to Kou were demoted or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 張崇貴，真定人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonggui, a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonggui was a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 太祖時為內中高品，稍遷殿頭。

translations.literal: During Taizu's reign he served as Inner-palace Senior Attendant, and gradually rose to Hall Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu he served as Inner-palace Senior Attendant and gradually rose to Hall Chief.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，以善射遷為禦帶。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo, for skill in archery he was promoted to Imperial Belt Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo reign, for his skill in archery he was promoted to Imperial Belt Guard.

sentences.zh: 錢俶納土，命馳往閱城防儲偫之數。

translations.literal: When Qian Chu submitted his territory, he was ordered to gallop there to inspect the numbers of city defenses and stored provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Chu submitted his territory, Chonggui was ordered to ride there at speed to inspect the city's defenses and stored provisions.

sentences.zh: 親征太原，從崔彥進、李漢瓊先路視水草。

translations.literal: On the personal campaign against Taiyuan, he followed Cui Yanjin and Li Hanqiong on the advance route to survey water and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's personal campaign against Taiyuan, he followed Cui Yanjin and Li Hanqiong on the advance route to survey water and fodder.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，補內供奉官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed Inner Attendant-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duangong reign he was appointed Inner Attendant-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，命乘傳之延州招羌戎之內附者，發庫錢犒給，以金幣賜酋領。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was ordered to travel by relay post to Yanzhou to recruit Qiang and Rong tribesmen who wished to submit, disburse treasury funds for rewards, and bestow gold and silks on tribal chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was ordered to travel by relay post to Yanzhou to recruit Qiang and Rong tribesmen seeking to submit. He was to disburse treasury funds as rewards and bestow gold and silks on tribal chiefs.

sentences.zh: 將行，轉內班右班押班，就命管勾鄜延屯兵，李繼隆討李繼遷，詔崇貴以延安兵掎角進討。

translations.literal: About to depart, he was promoted to Inner Corps Right Escort Chief, and concurrently appointed to manage the garrison troops of Bian and Yan; Li Jilong was campaigning against Li Jiqian—an edict ordered Chonggui to advance with Yan'an troops in pincer fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Just before his departure he was promoted to Inner Corps Right Escort Chief and concurrently appointed to manage the garrison troops of Bian and Yan. When Li Jilong was campaigning against Li Jiqian, an edict ordered Chonggui to advance with Yan'an troops in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 及擒趙保忠，留崇貴與石霸守綏州，徙平夏民以實之。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baozhong was captured, Chonggui was left with Shi Ba to guard Suizhou, and Pingxia people were moved to populate it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baozhong was captured, Chonggui was left with Shi Ba to hold Suizhou, and Pingxia settlers were moved there to fill it.

sentences.zh: 繼遷扼橐駝路，驅脅內屬戎人，崇貴與田敏率熟倉族乚遇戰於雙塠，殺二千餘級，掠牛羊、橐駝、鎧甲甚眾，連詔褒諭。

translations.literal: Jiqian blocked the Camel Road, coerced submissive tribesmen; Chonggui with Tian Min led the Shucang tribe Yi to encounter battle at Shuangduo, killed more than two thousand, plundered very many cattle, sheep, camels, and armor, and received consecutive edicts of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian blocked the Camel Road and coerced tribesmen who had submitted to the court. Chonggui and Tian Min led the Shucang tribesman Yi into battle at Shuangduo, killing more than two thousand enemies and seizing large numbers of cattle, sheep, camels, and armor. The court sent edict after edict praising their achievement.

sentences.zh: 繼遷走漠中，遣其將佐趙光祚、張浦求納款，會於石堡砦，崇貴椎牛釃酒犒諭之，給以錦袍帶。

translations.literal: Jiqian fled into the desert; he sent his generals Zhao Guangzuo and Zhang Pu to seek submission; they met at Shibao Fort; Chonggui slaughtered an ox and poured wine to feast and instruct them, granting brocade robes and belts.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian fled into the desert and sent his officers Zhao Guangzuo and Zhang Pu to offer submission. They met at Shibao Fort, where Chonggui slaughtered an ox and poured libations to feast and reassure them, granting brocade robes and belts.

sentences.zh: 會改內班為黃門，命為黃門右班押班，仍加內殿崇班，又改黃門為內侍，職隨易焉。

translations.literal: When the Inner Corps was renamed Yellow Gate, he was appointed Yellow Gate Right Escort Chief, and additionally made Inner Hall Honored Companion; when Yellow Gate was again renamed Inner Attendant, the office changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Inner Corps was renamed Yellow Gate, he was appointed Yellow Gate Right Escort Chief and additionally made Inner Hall Honored Companion. When Yellow Gate was renamed again as Inner Attendant, his title changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 既而繼遷貢橐駝、名馬待罪，遣崇貴往賜器幣、茶藥、衣物。

translations.literal: Soon Jiqian presented camels and fine horses to await judgment; Chonggui was sent to bestow vessels and silks, tea and medicine, and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jiqian presented camels and fine horses in submission. Chonggui was sent to bestow vessels and silks, tea and medicine, and clothing.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，進崇儀副使、內侍右班副都知。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao he was promoted to Deputy Honored Ceremonial Commissioner and Deputy Chief of the Inner Attendant Right Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao he was promoted to Deputy Honored Ceremonial Commissioner and Deputy Chief of the Inner Attendant Right Corps.

sentences.zh: 時繼遷復叛，劫芻饋於浦洛河。

translations.literal: At the time Jiqian rebelled again and plundered fodder at the Pulu River.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jiqian rebelled again and raided fodder supplies at the Pulu River.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔李繼隆大發師進討。

translations.literal: In the second year an edict ordered Li Jilong to raise a large force and advance in punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year an edict ordered Li Jilong to mobilize a large army and advance in punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 賊圍靈州急，太宗將棄之，廷議未決，命崇貴與馮納乘傳往議其事，乃益兵固守，就命為靈、環、慶州、清遠軍路監軍，又為排陣都監。

translations.literal: The enemy besieged Lingzhou urgently; Taizong was about to abandon it; court deliberation had not decided; Chonggui and Feng Na were ordered to travel by relay to discuss the matter; troops were increased to hold firm; he was concurrently appointed Military Inspector for the Ling, Huan, Qing prefectures and Qingyuan Army route, and also Array Deployment Director General.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pressed the siege of Lingzhou hard. Taizong was about to abandon the city, but court deliberation had not settled the matter. Chonggui and Feng Na were ordered to travel by relay post to discuss it. Reinforcements were sent to hold the city, and Chonggui was concurrently appointed Military Inspector for the Ling, Huan, and Qing prefectures and the Qingyuan Army route, and also Array Deployment Director General.

sentences.zh: 真宗立，拜洛苑使、右班都知、管勾并州軍馬。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he was appointed Luoyuan Commissioner, Chief of the Right Corps, and Acting Director of Bingzhou military horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne, Chonggui was appointed Luoyuan Commissioner, Chief of the Right Corps, and Acting Director of Bingzhou military horses.

sentences.zh: 自至道後，五路討賊，兵戰相繼，卒無成功。

translations.literal: From after Zhidao, five routes campaigned against the brigands; battles followed one after another, but in the end there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhidao period onward, campaigns against the rebels were launched on five routes. Battles followed one after another, but in the end none succeeded.

sentences.zh: 及是，保吉復修貢，詔以定難節度授之，命崇貴持詔命、衣帶、器幣以賜。

translations.literal: At this time Baoji again resumed tribute; an edict granted him the Dingnan Jiedushi; Chonggui was ordered to carry the edict, robes and belt, vessels and silks to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Baoji resumed tribute. An edict granted him the Dingnan Jiedushi, and Chonggui was ordered to carry the edict, robes and belt, and gifts of vessels and silks to bestow them.

sentences.zh: 使還，加六宅使。

translations.literal: On return from his mission he was made Commissioner of the Six Residences.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the mission he was made Commissioner of the Six Residences.

sentences.zh: 崇貴久在邊，善識羌戎情偽，西人畏服。

translations.literal: Chonggui long served on the frontier and knew well the true and false motives of Qiang and Rong; western peoples feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui had long served on the frontier and understood the true motives of the Qiang and Rong. The peoples of the west feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 每德明有所論述及境上交侵，皆先付裁制。

translations.literal: Whenever Deming made any declaration or border incursions occurred, matters were first entrusted to Chonggui for adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Deming sent communications or border clashes occurred, the matter was first entrusted to Chonggui for decision.

sentences.zh: 夏州趣邊有二路，其文移至環慶者，皆付延州議焉。

translations.literal: From Xiazhou toward the border there were two roads; official documents that went to Huan and Qing were all referred to Yanzhou for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiazhou toward the border there were two routes. Official documents bound for Huan and Qing were all referred to Yanzhou for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 嘗請置緣邊安撫使，如北面之制。

translations.literal: He once requested establishing frontier Pacification Commissioners, on the model of the northern frontier system.
translations.idiomatic: He once requested the establishment of frontier Pacification Commissioners on the model used on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「西鄙別無經營，苟德明能守富貴，無慮朝廷失恩信也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "On the western marches there is no other management needed; if Deming can keep his wealth and rank, there is no worry that the court will fail in grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The western frontier needs no special management. If Deming can hold on to his wealth and rank, there is no need to fear that the court will fail in grace and trust.

sentences.zh: 增置署局，徒為張皇，不若委卿靜製之。

translations.literal: To add offices and bureaus would only make empty display; better to entrust it to you to manage quietly.
translations.idiomatic: Adding offices and bureaus would only create needless alarm. Better to leave the matter quietly in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」二年，上言久去鄉里，願得告歸葬父母。

translations.literal: " In the second year he memorialized that having long been away from his homeland, he wished to obtain leave to return and bury his parents.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second year he memorialized that, having long been away from home, he wished to obtain leave to return and bury his parents.

sentences.zh: 許之，錫與甚厚。

translations.literal: It was granted; gifts and favors were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Permission was granted, and the emperor bestowed gifts and favors with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 復命為都鈐轄，提舉榷場。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to serve as Chief Controller and to supervise the monopoly markets.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Chief Controller and put in charge of the frontier trade markets.

sentences.zh: 崇貴乞留京師，面諭委屬之意，聽歲入奏事。

translations.literal: Chonggui requested to remain in the capital; the emperor received him in audience and instructed him in the duties entrusted to him, and permitted him to enter court each year to report on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui asked to remain in the capital. The emperor received him in audience, explained the duties entrusted to him, and allowed him to return to court each year to report on affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year he died, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 帝悼惜之，贈豐州觀察使，內侍護喪還京師。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned and regretted it; he was posthumously granted Observation Commissioner of Fengzhou; eunuchs escorted the funeral back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply. He was posthumously made Observation Commissioner of Fengzhou, and eunuchs escorted his coffin back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 子承素，東染院副使。

translations.literal: His son Chengsu served as Deputy Commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengsu held the post of Deputy Commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Bureau.

sentences.zh: 張繼能，字守拙，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jineng, courtesy name Shouzhuo, was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jineng, courtesy name Shouzhuo, was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父讚，晉末為內班。

translations.literal: His father Zan served as an Inner Corps attendant in the late Jin period.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zan had served as an Inner Corps attendant in the late Jin period.

sentences.zh: 繼能，建隆初以黃門事禁中，太平興國初為內品。

translations.literal: Jineng, at the beginning of Jianlong, served as a Yellow Gate attendant in the palace; at the start of Taiping Xingguo he became a Senior Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianlong era Jineng served as a Yellow Gate attendant in the palace; at the start of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to Senior Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從征河東，命主城南洞屋，以勞遷高品。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Hedong he was ordered to command the south-city cave dwellings; for his merit he was promoted to Senior Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Hedong he was ordered to command the south-city cave dwellings. For his service he was promoted to Senior Attendant.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，命為高陽、鎮、定路先鋒都監，從崔彥進戰長城口，多所俘馘。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, he was appointed Vanguard Director General for the Gaoyang, Zhen, and Ding route; following Cui Yanjin he fought at Changcheng Pass and took many captives and heads.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, he was appointed Vanguard Director General for the Gaoyang, Zhen, and Ding route. Following Cui Yanjin he fought at Changcheng Pass and took many captives and heads.

sentences.zh: 明年，又與彥進敗契丹於唐興口，轉殿頭高品。

translations.literal: The next year, together with Yanjin he defeated the Khitan at Tangxing Pass and was transferred to Palace Gate Senior Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he and Yanjin defeated the Khitan at Tangxing Pass, and Jineng was transferred to Palace Gate Senior Attendant.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，夏州叛命李繼隆為銀、夏都部署，以繼能監軍。

translations.literal: During the Yongxi era, when Xiazhou rebelled, Li Jilong was appointed Overall Deployment Commissioner for Yin and Xia; Jineng was made Military Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, when Xiazhou rebelled, Li Jilong was appointed Overall Deployment Commissioner for Yin and Xia, and Jineng was made Military Inspector.

sentences.zh: 俄徙護定州屯兵，領驍捷卒三千，屯五回嶺。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to oversee the garrison troops at Dingzhou, leading three thousand Swift and Keen soldiers stationed at Wuhui Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to oversee the garrison at Dingzhou, leading three thousand Swift and Keen soldiers stationed at Wuhui Ridge.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷入內殿頭，從趙保忠討李繼遷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was promoted to Inner Palace Gate Chief and followed Zhao Baozhong in campaigning against Li Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duangong era he was promoted to Inner Palace Gate Chief and followed Zhao Baozhong in campaigning against Li Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 保忠薦其有材，命與保忠同經略其事。

translations.literal: Baozhong recommended him as talented, and he was ordered to conduct strategic planning of the affair together with Baozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhong recommended him as talented, and he was ordered to manage the campaign jointly with Baozhong.

sentences.zh: 代還，掌內弓箭庫。

translations.literal: On return from his tour of duty he was put in charge of the Inner Bow and Arrow Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour of duty ended he was put in charge of the Inner Bow and Arrow Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，與白承睿護芻粟入靈武。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, together with Bai Chengrui he escorted fodder and grain into Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua he and Bai Chengrui escorted fodder and grain into Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 會繼遷復寇邊，命繼能、承睿與知靈州侯延廣領驍卒五千，同主軍務，俄留為本州都監。

translations.literal: When Jiqian again raided the border, Jineng, Chengrui, and Lingzhou prefect Hou Yanguang were ordered to lead five thousand elite soldiers to jointly manage military affairs; soon Jineng was retained as Director General of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqian again raided the border, Jineng, Chengrui, and Lingzhou prefect Hou Yanguang were ordered to lead five thousand elite soldiers in managing military affairs. Soon Jineng was retained as Director General of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及鄭文寶議城威州、清遠軍，繼能護其役。

translations.literal: When Zheng Wenbao proposed building fortifications at Weizhou and Qingyuan Army, Jineng oversaw the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Wenbao proposed building fortifications at Weizhou and Qingyuan Army, Jineng oversaw the construction.

sentences.zh: 工畢，命與西京作坊副使張延洲同知軍事，又與田紹斌同掌積石砦。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he was ordered to jointly manage military affairs with Western Capital Workshop Deputy Commissioner Zhang Yanzhou, and together with Tian Shaobin to manage Jishi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he was ordered to manage military affairs jointly with Western Capital Workshop Deputy Commissioner Zhang Yanzhou, and together with Tian Shaobin to command Jishi Fort.

sentences.zh: 就遷內供奉官、靈環慶、清遠軍後陣都監，與西人轉鬥，敗走之。

translations.literal: He was concurrently promoted to Inner Attendant-in-Waiting and Rear Array Director General for the Ling, Huan, Qing, and Qingyuan Army commands; he fought in repeated clashes with the western peoples and drove them off in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently promoted to Inner Attendant-in-Waiting and Rear Array Director General for the Ling, Huan, Qing, and Qingyuan Army commands. In repeated clashes with the western peoples he fought them off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 復還清遠。

translations.literal: He then returned to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 詣闕奏事，遷內殿崇班。

translations.literal: He went to court to report on affairs and was promoted to Inner Palace Honored Corps.
translations.idiomatic: He went to court to report on affairs and was promoted to Inner Palace Honored Corps.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜供備庫副使，復遣護環州屯兵，徙涇、原、儀、渭都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Provision Equipment Storehouse, again dispatched to oversee garrison troops at Huanzhou, and transferred to General Inspector of Jing, Yuan, Yi, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Provision Equipment Storehouse, again dispatched to oversee the garrison at Huanzhou, and transferred to General Inspector of Jing, Yuan, Yi, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷崇儀使、靈、環十州軍兵馬都監兼巡檢安撫使。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he was promoted to Honored Ceremonial Commissioner and made Military and Horse Director General for the ten prefectures and armies of Ling and Huan, concurrently Pacification and Inspection Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne, he was promoted to Honored Ceremonial Commissioner and made Military and Horse Director General for the ten prefectures and armies of Ling and Huan, concurrently serving as Pacification and Inspection Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年王均之亂，命為川峽兩路招安巡檢使。

translations.literal: During Wang Jun's rebellion in the third year of Xianping, he was appointed Pacification and Inspection Commissioner for the two Sichuan and Gorges routes.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Jun's rebellion in the third year of Xianping, he was appointed Pacification and Inspection Commissioner for the two Sichuan and Gorges routes.

sentences.zh: 成都平，留為利州招安巡檢，尋召歸。

translations.literal: When Chengdu was pacified, he was kept as Pacification Inspector at Lizhou, and soon recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu was pacified, he remained as Pacification Inspector at Lizhou and was soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 會銀、夏寇警，復為邠寧駐泊都監。

translations.literal: When alarms of raids arose from Yin and Xia, he was again made Garrison Director General at Binning.
translations.idiomatic: When raids from Yin and Xia raised alarms, he was again made Garrison Director General at Binning.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇清遠軍，營於積石河，繼能與楊瓊、馮守規在慶州逗留，不時赴援，致陷城堡，又焚棄青岡砦，特詔下御史府，免死，長流儋州。

translations.literal: The Tangut raided Qingyuan Army and encamped at the Jishi River. Jineng, Yang Qiong, and Feng Shougui lingered at Qingzhou and did not come to the rescue in time, causing the fortress to fall; they also abandoned and burned Qinggang Fort. By special edict the case was sent to the Censorate; death was commuted and he was exiled for life to Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut raided Qingyuan Army and encamped on the Jishi River. Jineng, Yang Qiong, and Feng Shougui lingered at Qingzhou and failed to arrive in time, allowing the fortress to fall. They also abandoned and burned Qinggang Fort. By special edict the case was referred to the Censorate. The death sentence was commuted and Jineng was exiled for life to Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，會赦，還為內侍省內常侍，又為陝西捕賊巡檢，獲千餘人，改內殿崇班。
